record.narrative: No assessments are due and voluntary validation capacity is exhausted, so this analyze stage focuses on the remaining untested active hypotheses in the supplied ledger. I select H247 because it is the direct female-stratified complement to the accepted male PTEN-loss STAT3 mean effect (H246) and the unresolved male interaction (H232), helping determine whether the PTEN-loss/STAT3 association remains internally robust in the sex strata. I then run the four missing/low-quality matched-omics robustness analyses H249-H252, testing whether the four core internal associations (SMARCA4 loss with SMARCA2 dependency, MSI-high with WRN dependency, KEAP1 loss with weaker NFE2L2 dependency, and PTEN loss with stronger STAT3 dependency) persist when has_rna_dna_crispr_qc=0. These are important because core effects could otherwise reflect selection in QC-passed cell lines. Next, I run H253-H256 to test context dependence in co-alteration and culture contexts: PTEN-loss STAT3 dependency among STK11-loss lines, KEAP1-loss NFE2L2 and SMARCA4-loss SMARCA2 among CDKN2A-loss lines, and MSI-high WRN dependency in high-serum media. Finally, I run the three new untested hypothesis comparisons H257-H259: MYC amplification versus WRN dependency, BRCA2 loss versus NFE2L2 dependency, and ARID1A loss versus STAT3 dependency. I do not select H248 because it duplicates H247 exactly. For direction -1 mean differences, a positive signed estimate indicates stronger dependency in the exposed group; for direction +1, a positive signed estimate indicates a less negative dependency score or the registered reverse contrast. Infeasible cells should be treated as noninformative rather than null. All selected analyses are unadjusted internal associations in this supplied lung-lineage dataset, not causal effects or externally generalizable predictions.

H247 remains active because the female-stratified PTEN-loss STAT3 mean difference is still untested; it is the most relevant remaining internal follow-up to interpret the unresolved male interaction H232.\n\nUsing the signed reporting convention used throughout this run: for direction -1 mean-difference claims, a positive estimate means the exposed group has a more negative dependency score, i.e. stronger dependency; for direction +1 claims, a positive estimate means a less negative score or a larger exposed-minus-comparator contrast depending on contrast; for interactions, a positive estimate means a larger exposed-minus-comparator contrast in the named subgroup than in its complement. I used approximately 0.10 dependency-score units as the practical relevance benchmark consistent with the run's 10% decision rule.\n\nThe strongest scientifically meaningful evidence in this supplied lung-lineage dataset supports four biomarker-dependency associations, not causal mechanisms or generalized therapeutic claims. First, SMARCA4 loss is associated with markedly stronger SMARCA2 dependency: discovery +0.784, 95% CI +0.765 to +0.803, R6, and independent validation +0.804, 95% CI +0.775 to +0.833, R53. Second, MSI-high status is associated with markedly stronger WRN dependency: discovery +0.790, 95% CI +0.760 to +0.819, R7, and validation +0.812, 95% CI +0.765 to +0.858, R40. Third, KEAP1 loss is associated with weaker NFE2L2 dependency, meaning a less negative dependency score, not stronger dependency: signed discovery +0.796, 95% CI +0.776 to +0.816, R8 signed to the accepted reverse-direction claim H13, and validation +0.791, 95% CI +0.763 to +0.820, R66. The originally registered stronger-dependency direction H8 is rejected. Fourth, PTEN loss is associated with stronger STAT3 dependency: discovery +0.267, 95% CI +0.215 to +0.319, R25, and validation +0.268, 95% CI +0.188 to +0.348, R26. This fourth effect is smaller than the first three but still clearly above the relevance benchmark and replicated in independent validation.\n\nThe core SMARCA4-loss and MSI-high effects are very large relative to the spread of the corresponding dependency scores and persist across many internal eligibility strata, including lineage subtype, CRISPR library, screen batch, screen-quality strata, matched omics availability, mutation burden, aneuploidy, growth-rate and culture strata, and several co-alteration strata. The core KEAP1-loss NFE2L2 effect similarly persisted across many contexts, including batch, subtype, Avana and KY library strata, screen-QC strata, adherent culture, lower mutation burden, aneuploidy strata, and several co-alteration strata. These are unadjusted stratified associations, not covariate-adjusted or causal effect-modification conclusions.\n\nA large number of biologically plausible direct or indirect predictor-outcome hypotheses were not supported. record.narrative: All newly delivered due comparisons have valid Welch results and sufficient cells. Using the run convention, for direction -1 mean differences a positive signed estimate means the exposed group has a more negative dependency score, i.e. stronger dependency; for the direction +1 KEAP1-loss NFE2L2 claim a positive signed estimate means weaker, less negative NFE2L2 dependency. I used approximately 0.10 dependency-score units as the relevance benchmark consistent with the run's 10% decision rule. H247 is accepted: in female lines, PTEN loss is associated with stronger STAT3 dependency (+0.237, 95% CI +0.156 to +0.318). This extends the accepted overall and male-stratified PTEN-loss STAT3 association to females, but it does not by itself establish a statistically supported sex interaction. H249-H252 accept the four core associations in the missing/low-quality matched-omics setting: SMARCA4 loss remains associated with much stronger SMARCA2 dependency, MSI-high with much stronger WRN dependency, KEAP1 loss with much weaker NFE2L2 dependency, and PTEN loss with stronger STAT3 dependency. This is an important technical robustness check because it shows the associations are not confined to QC-passed matched-omics samples, though they remain unadjusted internal associations rather than causal effects. H253-H256 accept robustness in selected co-alteration and culture contexts: PTEN-loss stronger STAT3 dependency among STK11-loss lines, KEAP1-loss weaker NFE2L2 dependency and SMARCA4-loss stronger SMARCA2 dependency among CDKN2A-loss lines, and MSI-high stronger WRN dependency under high-serum conditions. All intervals lie clearly above the relevance threshold and directionally match the core claims. The three new biological hypotheses do not support scientifically meaningful positive dependency associations. H257 is rejected because MYC amplification shows a small opposite-direction signed estimate for WRN dependency (-0.033, CI -0.064 to -0.002), not a clinically meaningful strengthening. H258 is rejected because BRCA2 loss on NFE2L2 dependency is near null with upper bound below threshold (+0.014, CI -0.051 to +0.079). H259 is rejected because ARID1A loss on STAT3 dependency is small and null-leaning (-0.013, CI -0.039 to +0.013). No leakage is apparent; these are measured-predictor to outcome comparisons. Residual confounding remains possible because all estimates are unadjusted and could be affected by library, batch, Cas9 activity, screen QC, ploidy/aneuploidy, mutation burden, subtype, culture, media, and co-alterations. Given multiplicity, only effects with intervals clearly above the relevance benchmark were accepted. Voluntary validation capacity is exhausted, so no validation request is made. H248 is an exact duplicate of H247; I did not create a separate conclusion for it to avoid double-counting the same canonical comparison. I registered low-Cas9-activity mean-difference tests of the four core associations as the next high-value internal follow-up because Cas9 efficiency is a plausible technical modifier not fully covered by prior screen-quality and matched-omics checks.

record.narrative: No new validation was delivered and no validation response deadline is open because voluntary validation capacity is exhausted. I therefore make no evidence-based change to accepted or rejected claims in this synthesis. The supported internal findings in the supplied lung-lineage CRISPR dataset remain four associations, using signed reporting: SMARCA4 loss is associated with markedly stronger SMARCA2 dependency, signed discovery +0.784 and validation +0.804; MSI-high status is associated with markedly stronger WRN dependency, signed discovery +0.790 and validation +0.812; KEAP1 loss is associated with weaker NFE2L2 dependency, i.e. a less negative dependency score, signed reverse claim +0.796 and validation +0.791, while the original stronger dependency direction remains rejected; PTEN loss is associated with stronger STAT3 dependency, signed discovery +0.267 and validation +0.268. These effects are not causal claims and should not be treated as externally transportable therapeutic predictions. Negative findings include the simplest matched oncogene dependencies: KRAS mutation with KRAS dependency, BRAF V600E with BRAF dependency, EGFR amplification with EGFR dependency after validation, ERBB2 amplification with ERBB2 dependency, TP53 loss with MDM2 dependency, and MYC amplification with several candidate dependencies such as USP7, DHX9, POLR2A, KRAS, MDM2, STAT3, and RPL11 in the tested settings. ARID1A loss independent of SMARCA4 loss was not supported for SMARCA2 dependency, and RB1 loss with POLR2A dependency was rejected after validation. Unresolved uncertainty is mostly effect modification: male PTEN-loss STAT3 interaction, near-median growth interaction, older-age attenuation interaction, and some small-cell interaction estimates remain inconclusive rather than null. Low Cas9 activity is the next high value internal technical check, and claims H260 to H263 remain active. I register one additional PTEN-loss STAT3 interaction in female lines because the female mean effect was accepted while only the male interaction has been tested. This will help determine whether PTEN-loss STAT3 dependency is broadly present or sex-context dependent.

For H264, a positive signed interaction estimate indicates the PTEN-loss contrast is more in the claimed direction among females than among the complement. Study instructions:
Investigate diverse, scientifically meaningful comparisons and use previous
results to allocate further investigation. Broad exploration and focused follow-up are both useful
throughout the run. Assess discoveries in this supplied dataset and use independent validation when

Register comparisons, anticipated directions, and initial assessments before requesting analyses.
The controller assigns claim references. For a changed claim, propose a new comparison and link
refinements to the earlier parent claim.
Clinical log_pfs_months is natural log progression-free survival in months, fully observed without
censoring. Dependency scores are continuous; more negative values mean stronger dependency.
Research signatures are constructed standardized assays in arbitrary units. Research markers D, E,
and F are constructed binary assays with no assigned gene, pathway, or clinical role.
A mean_difference is exposed minus comparator within eligibility and subgroup. An interaction
subtracts that comparison in the subgroup complement in the same eligible population.
Use your scientific judgment to assess the size, uncertainty, and importance of each effect
and decide which conclusions the evidence supports. Explain your reasoning in the narrative.
Returned estimates and intervals are ALREADY SIGNED to the indicated hypothesis direction. Do not
multiply them by direction again. For example, raw -0.4 with direction -1 is reported as +0.4.
Discovery analyses use 95% Welch intervals and need at least 20 observations in every
comparison cell.

Each iteration has explore, analyze, appraise, and synthesize stages. Every stage may register
hypotheses for later analysis. Analyze selects up to 12 previously registered hypotheses.
Appraise assesses every new discovery result, records active/deferred/closed investigation, and may
request validation after considering those results. At most one new voluntary validation request
is allowed per iteration and ten per run. Cached requests reuse the same evidence. The evaluator
may also deliver scheduled validation during the run. Independent intervals account for the maximum
number of validation comparisons in the run. Results arrive before synthesis. Assess newly released
validation immediately in synthesis and explicitly reassess the original claim when its response
deadline appears in the context, even if you also investigate a refinement. The controller maintains
the accepted claim set from your assessments; you do not need to repeat that list. Explanations are
retained for inspection. Acceptance does not require prior independent validation.


You are investigating the supplied research dataset. Return one JSON object using
only this stage's response form. The service performs analyses; you choose the science.
For this task, a relative difference in outcome of 10% or greater is considered clinically significant.
Use your judgment about uncertainty and conclusions in light of this clinical significance threshold. Acceptance does not require
independent validation first. Explain your reasoning in narrative.

The ledger contains every registered claim, its current assessment, and all its available direct
evidence. References H1, H2, ... identify claims; R1, R2, ... identify evidence. Copy these short
references when needed. New proposals receive references automatically after this stage. A changed
comparison or reversed claim is a new proposal, optionally linked to an existing parent.

expectation
of the raw exposed-minus-comparator contrast before seeing evidence (-1, 0 uncertain, +1).
initial_status is your assessment at registration. These initial judgments are recorded once.
If a proposal repeats an existing claim, the controller preserves that claim's current assessment;
use assessments to change a scientific conclusion.

For each claim in assessments_due, return one assessment with claim,
status (accept/reject/unresolved),
and investigation (active/deferred/closed). You may also reassess other claims. Omitted claims keep
their current assessment. Assess the original claim even when proposing a refinement or reversal.

the controller attaches those references. To specify a subset or related evidence, provide evidence
with short R references; include the evidence listed in assessments_due for that claim.
An unchanged assessment or an investigation-only change can use evidence: [];
changing accept/reject/unresolved requires available evidence. Bookkeeping does not satisfy a due
evidence assessment.
For a refinement, parent identifies the earlier claim; omitted motivating_evidence attaches the
parent's displayed evidence. These automatic links record evidence supplied for your assessment
or refinement, not proof that you discussed or understood every result.

The controller maintains the accepted set from your assessments. Do not reconstruct it. Optional
research_notes replaces your persistent notebook; omit it to keep the existing notes. Use it for
plans or reasoning worth retaining. Latest stage narratives are also retained. All earlier numerical
evidence remains in the ledger. Do not repeat completed actions or old responses.
Omit unused fields.

Your action now: Assess the newly delivered discovery evidence. Optionally set validate to one eligible claim reference for independent validation; omit it for no request. The controller attaches the discovery result. Validation arrives after this stage.

record.narrative: All newly due comparisons have valid Welch results and sufficient comparison cells. I retained the run convention that, for direction -1 mean differences, a positive signed estimate means stronger dependency in the exposed group, whereas for the direction +1 KEAP1-loss/dependency_NFE2L2 claim a positive signed estimate means weaker, less negative NFE2L2 dependency. I used about 0.10 dependency-score units as the practical relevance benchmark and accepted only intervals clearly above that threshold in the registered direction. H260-H263 are the low-Cas9-activity internal robustness tests of the four core associations: SMARCA4 loss with much stronger SMARCA2 dependency, MSI-high status with much stronger WRN dependency, KEAP1 loss with much weaker NFE2L2 dependency, and PTEN loss with stronger STAT3 dependency. All four are accepted: signed effect estimates are 0.754, 0.798, 0.799, and 0.372, and all lower confidence bounds are far above the 0.10 benchmark. H265-H268 are the corresponding high-Cas9-activity tests and are also accepted, with signed estimates 0.788, 0.776, 0.800, and 0.257 and lower bounds above the benchmark. Together these mean-difference results support the internal robustness of the four core associations when Cas9 activity is likely low versus likely adequate; they do not establish Cas9 activity as a causal modifier or prove external generalizability, and interaction evidence remains the more direct assessment of modification. H264 tests a female-specific PTEN-loss/STAT3 interaction. The signed estimate is small and opposite the claimed female-strengthening direction (-0.049; 95% CI -0.154 to 0.057), and the upper bound is below the 0.10 relevance threshold in the claimed direction. Therefore I reject this registered female-specific interaction hypothesis. This does not establish a meaningful opposite attenuation; the interval remains compatible with a small attenuation, but the evidence is insufficient to claim a clinically meaningful female-specific modification. H273 tests KEAP1 loss among faster-growing lines for NFE2L2 dependency and is accepted: signed estimate 0.835 with lower bound 0.793. This strengthens the direct association in that growth context, although the earlier interaction test remains unresolved because it lacks precise evidence for differential effect. H275 and H276 test whether MYC amplification has a masked effect on WRN or POLR2A dependency within MYC-high-expressing cell lines. Both are rejected: signed estimates are -0.030 and -0.010, upper bounds 0.015 and 0.021, below the 0.10 claimed-direction benchmark. The small negative signed estimates suggest no positive dependency association; if anything, point estimates are null-to-slightly opposite, but confidence intervals do not support a clinically meaningful opposite effect either. Residual concerns remain: these are unadjusted associations, Cas9-activity-restricted analyses depend on observed Cas9 scores and could be subject to selection or technical confounding, and many comparisons were tested. I therefore only accepted results with intervals decisively above the practical relevance benchmark. Voluntary validation capacity is exhausted, so I make no validation request.

I therefore make no accept or reject change based on new validation evidence. The strongest supported internal associations in the supplied lung-lineage CRISPR dataset remain four: SMARCA4 loss with much stronger SMARCA2 dependency, signed discovery estimate R6 plus 0.784 with validation R53 plus 0.804; MSI-high status with much stronger WRN dependency, R7 plus 0.790 with validation R40 plus 0.812; KEAP1 loss with weaker NFE2L2 dependency in the reverse claim H13, R8 plus 0.796 with validation R66 plus 0.791; and PTEN loss with stronger STAT3 dependency, R25 plus 0.267 with validation R26 plus 0.268. All have lower confidence limits far above the 0.10 dependency-score practical benchmark and are repeatedly reproduced in prespecified internal strata. The original stronger KEAP1-loss NFE2L2 dependency direction remains rejected because the exposed-minus-comparator difference is positive, meaning KEAP1-loss cell lines have less negative and therefore weaker NFE2L2 dependency. Negative or near-null findings include the simplest matched genotype-dependency hypotheses: KRAS mutation with KRAS dependency, BRAF V600E with BRAF dependency, EGFR amplification with EGFR dependency, ERBB2 amplification with ERBB2 dependency, TP53 loss with MDM2 dependency, and MYC amplification with several tested dependencies. ARID1A loss independent of SMARCA4 loss was not supported for SMARCA2 dependency, and RB1 loss with POLR2A dependency was rejected after validation. These negative findings should be interpreted as absence of a scientifically meaningful association in this dataset, not proof that no effect could exist in all contexts. Residual uncertainty is concentrated in effect modification: many interactions across Cas9 activity, culture type, screen batch, growth rate, age, sex, EMT, hypoxia, copy-number states, and expression assays are imprecise or null, so main-effect robustness should not be overinterpreted as homogeneity across biological contexts. High ploidy and KY-library WRN effects remain active but untested. The most informative next analyses are the already active high-ploidy mean-difference checks H269-H272 and KY-library WRN H274, plus the newly registered high-ploidy interaction tests for SMARCA2, WRN, NFE2L2, and STAT3. These interaction tests are important because a persistent subgroup mean effect by itself does not establish that ploidy modifies the association. If high-ploidy interactions prove informative, low-ploidy complement estimates will be the logical follow-up. No validation requests are available. All conclusions remain internal unadjusted associations in the supplied lung-lineage dataset and are not causal effects or externally transportable therapeutic predictions.

record.narrative: No claims are due for assessment, and voluntary validation capacity is exhausted, so this exploration only registers prespecified internal-association refinements that complete the current ploidy robustness program in the supplied lung-lineage CRISPR dataset. The scientific focus is whether the four strong internal associations already supported in the full dataset and many internal strata are present in the low-ploidy complement of the high-ploidy context, where ploidy <= 3.0 is used as the low-ploidy eligibility criterion. The exposures and outcomes are the four core pairs: SMARCA4 loss with dependency_SMARCA2, MSI-high status with dependency_WRN, KEAP1 loss with dependency_NFE2L2 in the reverse claim direction, and PTEN loss with dependency_STAT3. For the three direction -1 mean-difference claims, I anticipate a raw exposed-minus-comparator difference below zero because a more negative dependency score means stronger dependency in the exposed group. For the direction +1 KEAP1-loss/dependency_NFE2L2 claim, I anticipate a raw difference above zero because the accepted internal finding is that KEAP1-loss cell lines have weaker, less negative NFE2L2 dependency. The alternatives are that the association is absent in low-ploidy cell lines, is below the conservative practical benchmark of about 0.10 dependency-score units, or reverses direction. These claims test whether the core effects occur in low-ploidy lines and complement the active high-ploidy mean tests and high-ploidy interaction tests. They should not be interpreted as causal claims or externally transportable therapeutic predictions.

record.narrative: No assessments are due in this analyze step, and voluntary validation capacity is exhausted, so the highest-value action is to test the active prespecified ploidy robustness and modification claims already registered. I selected the four high-ploidy interaction tests first (H277-H280) because interaction evidence is more directly informative than stratum-specific mean effects when asking whether ploidy modifies the association. H277 tests whether the SMARCA4-loss association with SMARCA2 dependency is stronger in high-ploidy cell lines than in the ploidy complement; H278 does the same for MSI-high status and WRN dependency; H279 does the same for the registered reverse KEAP1-loss/NFE2L2 association, where positive signed estimates correspond to weaker NFE2L2 dependency in the claimed direction; and H280 does the same for PTEN-loss/STAT3 dependency. For these interaction claims, a positive signed estimate means the exposed-minus-comparator contrast in the high-ploidy subgroup is more in the registered direction than the corresponding contrast in the complement, while a negative signed estimate means the opposite. I then selected the four high-ploidy mean-difference tests (H269-H272) to determine whether each core association remains present among high-ploidy cell lines. Finally, I selected the four low-ploidy mean complements (H281-H284) to test whether the same associations persist in the complementary low-ploidy context. Together these 12 tests address three scientifically distinct patterns: (1) the core association is present and similar in both ploidy groups with approximately null ploidy interactions, which would support internal robustness across ploidy; (2) the association is present primarily in high ploidy with a positive ploidy interaction, which would support high-ploidy modification or concentration; or (3) the high-ploidy means are present but the interaction is null because the low-ploidy complement is underpowered or imprecise. Practical relevance was assessed using the same conservative benchmark as earlier in the run: about 0.10 dependency-score units. A main effect or interaction should be considered scientifically meaningful only if its signed point estimate and confidence interval are clearly above that benchmark in the registered direction. Infeasible cells or insufficient-cell diagnostics will be treated as noninformative rather than evidence of absence. All conclusions remain unadjusted internal associations in the supplied lung-lineage CRISPR dataset, not causal claims or externally transportable therapeutic predictions.

Research goal: investigate which measured predictors and subgroups are associated with scientifically meaningful differences in dependency_BRAF (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_DHX9 (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_EGFR (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_ERBB2 (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_KIF18A (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_KRAS (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_MDM2 (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_NFE2L2 (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_POLR2A (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_RIT1 (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_RPL11 (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_SMARCA2 (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_STAT3 (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_TMED10 (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_USP7 (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_WRN (CRISPR dependency score). Use the supplied dataset to discover and follow up comparisons, assess effect sizes and uncertainty, and decide which conclusions the evidence supports. Use independent validation when useful and distinguish findings in this dataset from claims about causality or generalizability.
Each iteration proceeds through explore (propose comparisons), analyze (request tests), appraise (assess the resulting discovery evidence and optionally request validation), and synthesize (assess validation and update conclusions and plans).

Study instructions:
Investigate diverse, scientifically meaningful comparisons and use previous
results to allocate further investigation. Broad exploration and focused follow-up are both useful
throughout the run. Assess discoveries in this supplied dataset and use independent validation when
useful. Biological interpretation and generalizability may remain uncertain.

Register comparisons, anticipated directions, and initial assessments before requesting analyses.
The controller assigns claim references. For a changed claim, propose a new comparison and link
refinements to the earlier parent claim.
Clinical log_pfs_months is natural log progression-free survival in months, fully observed without
censoring. Dependency scores are continuous; more negative values mean stronger dependency.
Research signatures are constructed standardized assays in arbitrary units. Research markers D, E,
and F are constructed binary assays with no assigned gene, pathway, or clinical role.
A mean_difference is exposed minus comparator within eligibility and subgroup. An interaction
subtracts that comparison in the subgroup complement in the same eligible population.
Use your scientific judgment to assess the size, uncertainty, and importance of each effect
and decide which conclusions the evidence supports. Explain your reasoning in the narrative.
Returned estimates and intervals are ALREADY SIGNED to the indicated hypothesis direction. Do not
multiply them by direction again. For example, raw -0.4 with direction -1 is reported as +0.4.
Discovery analyses use 95% Welch intervals and need at least 20 observations in every
comparison cell.

Each iteration has explore, analyze, appraise, and synthesize stages. Every stage may register
hypotheses for later analysis. Analyze selects up to 12 previously registered hypotheses.
Appraise assesses every new discovery result, records active/deferred/closed investigation, and may
request validation after considering those results. At most one new voluntary validation request
is allowed per iteration and ten per run. Cached requests reuse the same evidence. The evaluator
may also deliver scheduled validation during the run. Independent intervals account for the maximum
number of validation comparisons in the run. Results arrive before synthesis. Assess newly released
validation immediately in synthesis and explicitly reassess the original claim when its response
deadline appears in the context, even if you also investigate a refinement. The controller maintains
the accepted claim set from your assessments; you do not need to repeat that list. Explanations are
retained for inspection. Acceptance does not require prior independent validation.


You are investigating the supplied research dataset. Return one JSON object using
only this stage's response form. The service performs analyses; you choose the science.
For this task, a relative difference in outcome of 10% or greater is considered clinically significant.
Use your judgment about uncertainty and conclusions in light of this clinical significance threshold. Acceptance does not require
independent validation first. Explain your reasoning in narrative.

The ledger contains every registered claim, its current assessment, and all its available direct
evidence. References H1, H2, ... identify claims; R1, R2, ... identify evidence. Copy these short
references when needed. New proposals receive references automatically after this stage. A changed
comparison or reversed claim is a new proposal, optionally linked to an existing parent.
Proposal direction is the claim (+1 positive, -1 negative); anticipated_direction is your
expectation
of the raw exposed-minus-comparator contrast before seeing evidence (-1, 0 uncertain, +1).
initial_status is your assessment at registration. These initial judgments are recorded once.
If a proposal repeats an existing claim, the controller preserves that claim's current assessment;
use assessments to change a scientific conclusion.

For each claim in assessments_due, return one assessment with claim,
status (accept/reject/unresolved),
and investigation (active/deferred/closed). You may also reassess other claims. Omitted claims keep
their current assessment. Assess the original claim even when proposing a refinement or reversal.
By omitting evidence in an assessment, you assess all evidence displayed on that claim's card;
the controller attaches those references. To specify a subset or related evidence, provide evidence
with short R references; include the evidence listed in assessments_due for that claim.
An unchanged assessment or an investigation-only change can use evidence: [];
changing accept/reject/unresolved requires available evidence. Bookkeeping does not satisfy a due
evidence assessment.
For a refinement, parent identifies the earlier claim; omitted motivating_evidence attaches the
parent's displayed evidence. These automatic links record evidence supplied for your assessment
or refinement, not proof that you discussed or understood every result.

The controller maintains the accepted set from your assessments. Do not reconstruct it. Optional
research_notes replaces your persistent notebook; omit it to keep the existing notes. Use it for
plans or reasoning worth retaining. Latest stage narratives are also retained. All earlier numerical
evidence remains in the ledger. Do not repeat completed actions or old responses.
Omit unused fields.

Your action now: Assess the newly delivered discovery evidence. Optionally set validate to one eligible claim reference for independent validation; omit it for no request. The controller attaches the discovery result. Validation arrives after this stage.

record.narrative: All twelve new Welch comparisons are valid and have sufficient comparison cells. For direction -1 claims, a positive signed estimate means stronger, more negative dependency in the exposed group; for the direction +1 KEAP1-loss/dependency_NFE2L2 comparisons, a positive signed estimate means weaker, less negative NFE2L2 dependency in KEAP1-loss lines. I used 0.10 dependency-score units as a conservative practical-relevance benchmark because dependency scores are signed and often near zero, making percent-of-comparator interpretation unstable; the accepted core effects are also far larger than a 10% relative scale. The high-ploidy mean effects H269-H272 are accepted: SMARCA4 loss is associated with much stronger SMARCA2 dependency (signed estimate 0.762; 95% lower bound 0.726), MSI-high status with much stronger WRN dependency (0.788; lower bound 0.732), KEAP1 loss with much weaker NFE2L2 dependency (0.802; lower bound 0.763), and PTEN loss with stronger STAT3 dependency (0.243; lower bound 0.145), all well above the practical benchmark in the high-ploidy stratum. The ploidy<=3.0 mean effects H281-H284 are also accepted: SMARCA4 loss/SMARCA2 (0.792; lower bound 0.769), MSI-high/WRN (0.790; lower bound 0.755), KEAP1 loss/NFE2L2 reverse (0.794; lower bound 0.770), and PTEN loss/STAT3 (0.277; lower bound 0.215). These ploidy<=3.0 analyses overlap the ploidy>=3.0 analyses at exactly ploidy=3.0, so they should be interpreted as a broad low-like ploidy stratum rather than an exact disjoint complement of high ploidy. The four high-ploidy interaction claims H277-H280 are rejected: the signed interaction estimates are close to zero and their upper signed 95% bounds are below the 0.10 claimed-direction benchmark (SMARCA2/SMARCA4-loss 0.012; WRN/MSI-high 0.063; NFE2L2/KEAP1-loss 0.054; STAT3/PTEN-loss 0.082). Thus, there is no evidence that high ploidy strengthens the four core associations. This is not equivalence to null: the intervals include zero, and the STAT3/PTEN-loss interaction interval extends into the opposite direction beyond the practical threshold, so a possible high-ploidy attenuation remains unresolved. Multiplicity, unadjusted confounding, and inclusive ploidy boundaries remain limitations, but the accepted main effects are large, precise, and repeatedly reproduced across many prespecified internal strata. The interaction rejections are therefore best read as lack of support for claimed high-ploidy effect modification, not proof of complete homogeneity. Validation budget is exhausted, so no independent validation is requested; conclusions remain internal unadjusted associations in the supplied lung-lineage CRISPR dataset, not causal effects or externally transportable predictions. I also reopened H14 to allow a future test of SMARCA4 loss and dependency_SMARCA2 within adenocarcinoma, completing the subgroup coverage for the four core associations if capacity permits.

Study instructions:
Investigate diverse, scientifically meaningful comparisons and use previous

The controller assigns claim references. For a changed claim, propose a new comparison and link

Clinical log_pfs_months is natural log progression-free survival in months, fully observed without
censoring. Dependency scores are continuous; more negative values mean stronger dependency.
Research signatures are constructed standardized assays in arbitrary units. Research markers D, E,
and F are constructed binary assays with no assigned gene, pathway, or clinical role.
A mean_difference is exposed minus comparator within eligibility and subgroup. An interaction
subtracts that comparison in the subgroup complement in the same eligible population.
Use your scientific judgment to assess the size, uncertainty, and importance of each effect
and decide which conclusions the evidence supports. Explain your reasoning in the narrative.

comparison cell.

hypotheses for later analysis. Analyze selects up to 12 previously registered hypotheses.

request validation after considering those results. At most one new voluntary validation request
is allowed per iteration and ten per run. Cached requests reuse the same evidence. The evaluator
may also deliver scheduled validation during the run. Independent intervals account for the maximum
number of validation comparisons in the run. Results arrive before synthesis. Assess newly released

  "narrative": "No validation response deadlines are present and the voluntary validation budget is exhausted, so this synthesis does not change accepted claim statuses on the basis of new validation. The scientific conclusion is that the supplied 2000-line lung-lineage CRISPR dataset supports four scientifically meaningful internal associations between measured predictors and CRISPR dependency scores, with strong discovery effects and independent validation for the primary estimates. Dependency scores are signed such that more negative values mean stronger dependency; for direction -1 claims, a positive signed estimate means stronger exposed dependency, while for the KEAP1-loss/NFE2L2 reverse claim H13, a positive signed estimate means weaker NFE2L2 dependency in KEAP1-loss lines.

Supported core associations:

1. SMARCA4 loss is associated with much stronger SMARCA2 dependency. This is the accepted claim H6 with discovery R6 signed estimate +0.784, 95% Welch interval 0.765 to 0.803, and independent validation R53 signed estimate +0.804, interval 0.775 to 0.833. The effect is far above the practical benchmark of about 0.10 dependency-score units and is reproduced in many internal strata, including screen batch, CRISPR library, matched omics QC, screen quality, ploidy strata, mutation burden, Cas9 activity, age, and co-mutation-negative strata. The robustness across strata supports internal association and not causal therapeutic targeting.

2. MSI-high status is associated with much stronger WRN dependency. This is accepted claim H7 with discovery R7 signed estimate +0.790, interval 0.760 to 0.819, and validation R40 signed estimate +0.812, interval 0.765 to 0.858. The effect is extremely large relative to the dependency-scale benchmark. It is also robust across many internal strata, although prespecified effect-modification tests did not establish a reliable context-specific interaction. For example, H112 initially suggested a culture-related interaction for WRN/MSI-high, but validation reversed and the interval included zero, so it was rejected.

3. KEAP1 loss is associated with weaker NFE2L2 dependency, not stronger dependency. The original direction in H8 is rejected because the raw exposed-minus-comparator difference has the opposite sign. The reverse claim H13 is accepted using discovery R8 signed estimate +0.796, interval 0.776 to 0.816, and validation R66 signed estimate +0.791, interval 0.763 to 0.820. Interpreted biologically within this dataset, KEAP1-loss cell lines have less negative, therefore weaker, NFE2L2 dependency than KEAP1-intact lines. This remains an internal association and should not be described as a causal pathway effect without external mechanistic validation.

4. PTEN loss is associated with stronger STAT3 dependency. No validation response deadlines are present and the voluntary validation budget is exhausted, so this synthesis does not change accepted claim statuses on the basis of new validation. The scientific conclusion is that the supplied 2000-line lung-lineage CRISPR dataset supports four scientifically meaningful internal associations between measured predictors and CRISPR dependency scores, with strong discovery effects and independent validation for the primary estimates. Dependency scores are signed such that more negative values mean stronger dependency; for direction -1 claims, a positive signed estimate means stronger exposed dependency, while for the KEAP1-loss/NFE2L2 reverse claim H13, a positive signed estimate means weaker NFE2L2 dependency in KEAP1-loss lines.

Supported core associations:

1. SMARCA4 loss is associated with much stronger SMARCA2 dependency. This is the accepted claim H6 with discovery R6 signed estimate +0.784, 95% Welch interval 0.765 to 0.803, and independent validation R53 signed estimate +0.804, interval 0.775 to 0.833. The effect is far above the practical benchmark of about 0.10 dependency-score units and is reproduced in many internal strata, including screen batch, CRISPR library, matched omics QC, screen quality, ploidy strata, mutation burden, Cas9 activity, age, and co-mutation-negative strata. The robustness across strata supports internal association and not causal therapeutic targeting.

2. MSI-high status is associated with much stronger WRN dependency. This is accepted claim H7 with discovery R7 signed estimate +0.790, interval 0.760 to 0.819, and validation R40 signed estimate +0.812, interval 0.765 to 0.858. The effect is extremely large relative to the dependency-scale benchmark. It is also robust across many internal strata, although prespecified effect-modification tests did not establish a reliable context-specific interaction. For example, H112 initially suggested a culture-related interaction for WRN/MSI-high, but validation reversed and the interval included zero, so it was rejected.

3. KEAP1 loss is associated with weaker NFE2L2 dependency, not stronger dependency. The original direction in H8 is rejected because the raw exposed-minus-comparator difference has the opposite sign. The reverse claim H13 is accepted using discovery R8 signed estimate +0.796, interval 0.776 to 0.816, and validation R66 signed estimate +0.791, interval 0.763 to 0.820. Interpreted biologically within this dataset, KEAP1-loss cell lines have less negative, therefore weaker, NFE2L2 dependency than KEAP1-intact lines. This remains an internal association and should not be described as a causal pathway effect without external mechanistic validation.

4. PTEN loss is associated with stronger STAT3 dependency. This is accepted claim H41 with discovery R25 signed estimate +0.267, interval 0.215 to 0.319, and validation R26 signed estimate +0.268, interval 0.188 to 0.348. The effect is smaller than the SMARCA2, WRN, and NFE2L2 effects but is consistently above the 0.10 practical benchmark in the primary and many stratum analyses. Iteration 23/25, stage explore, attempt 1.
Research goal: investigate which measured predictors and subgroups are associated with scientifically meaningful differences in dependency_BRAF (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_DHX9 (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_EGFR (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_ERBB2 (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_KIF18A (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_KRAS (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_MDM2 (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_NFE2L2 (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_POLR2A (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_RIT1 (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_RPL11 (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_SMARCA2 (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_STAT3 (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_TMED10 (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_USP7 (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_WRN (CRISPR dependency score). Use the supplied dataset to discover and follow up comparisons, assess effect sizes and uncertainty, and decide which conclusions the evidence supports. Use independent validation when useful and distinguish findings in this dataset from claims about causality or generalizability.
Each iteration proceeds through explore (propose comparisons), analyze (request tests), appraise (assess the resulting discovery evidence and optionally request validation), and synthesize (assess validation and update conclusions and plans).

Study instructions:
Investigate diverse, scientifically meaningful comparisons and use previous
results to allocate further investigation. Broad exploration and focused follow-up are both useful
throughout the run. Assess discoveries in this supplied dataset and use independent validation when
useful. Biological interpretation and generalizability may remain uncertain.

Register comparisons, anticipated directions, and initial assessments before requesting analyses.
The controller assigns claim references. For a changed claim, propose a new comparison and link
refinements to the earlier parent claim.
Clinical log_pfs_months is natural log progression-free survival in months, fully observed without
censoring. Dependency scores are continuous; more negative values mean stronger dependency.
Research signatures are constructed standardized assays in arbitrary units. Research markers D, E,
and F are constructed binary assays with no assigned gene, pathway, or clinical role.
A mean_difference is exposed minus comparator within eligibility and subgroup. An interaction
subtracts that comparison in the subgroup complement in the same eligible population.
Use your scientific judgment to assess the size, uncertainty, and importance of each effect
and decide which conclusions the evidence supports. Explain your reasoning in the narrative.
Returned estimates and intervals are ALREADY SIGNED to the indicated hypothesis direction. Do not
multiply them by direction again. For example, raw -0.4 with direction -1 is reported as +0.4.
Discovery analyses use 95% Welch intervals and need at least 20 observations in every
comparison cell.

Each iteration has explore, analyze, appraise, and synthesize stages. Every stage may register
hypotheses for later analysis. Analyze selects up to 12 previously registered hypotheses.
Appraise assesses every new discovery result, records active/deferred/closed investigation, and may
request validation after considering those results. At most one new voluntary validation request
is allowed per iteration and ten per run. Cached requests reuse the same evidence. The evaluator
may also deliver scheduled validation during the run. Independent intervals account for the maximum
number of validation comparisons in the run. Results arrive before synthesis. Assess newly released
validation immediately in synthesis and explicitly reassess the original claim when its response
deadline appears in the context, even if you also investigate a refinement. The controller maintains
the accepted claim set from your assessments; you do not need to repeat that list. Explanations are
retained for inspection. Acceptance does not require prior independent validation.


You are investigating the supplied research dataset. Return one JSON object using
only this stage's response form. The service performs analyses; you choose the science.
For this task, a relative difference in outcome of 10% or greater is considered clinically significant.
Use your judgment about uncertainty and conclusions in light of this clinical significance threshold. Acceptance does not require
independent validation first. Explain your reasoning in narrative.

The ledger contains every registered claim, its current assessment, and all its available direct
evidence. References H1, H2, ... identify claims; R1, R2, ... identify evidence. Copy these short
references when needed. New proposals receive references automatically after this stage. A changed
comparison or reversed claim is a new proposal, optionally linked to an existing parent.
Proposal direction is the claim (+1 positive, -1 negative); anticipated_direction is your
expectation
of the raw exposed-minus-comparator contrast before seeing evidence (-1, 0 uncertain, +1).
initial_status is your assessment at registration. These initial judgments are recorded once.
If a proposal repeats an existing claim, the controller preserves that claim's current assessment;
use assessments to change a scientific conclusion.

For each claim in assessments_due, return one assessment with claim,
status (accept/reject/unresolved),
and investigation (active/deferred/closed). You may also reassess other claims. Omitted claims keep
their current assessment. Assess the original claim even when proposing a refinement or reversal.
By omitting evidence in an assessment, you assess all evidence displayed on that claim's card;
the controller attaches those references. To specify a subset or related evidence, provide evidence
with short R references; include the evidence listed in assessments_due for that claim.
An unchanged assessment or an investigation-only change can use evidence: [];
changing accept/reject/unresolved requires available evidence. Bookkeeping does not satisfy a due
evidence assessment.
For a refinement, parent identifies the earlier claim; omitted motivating_evidence attaches the
parent's displayed evidence. These automatic links record evidence supplied for your assessment
or refinement, not proof that you discussed or understood every result.

The controller maintains the accepted set from your assessments. Do not reconstruct it. Optional
research_notes replaces your persistent notebook; omit it to keep the existing notes. Use it for
plans or reasoning worth retaining. Latest stage narratives are also retained. All earlier numerical
evidence remains in the ledger. Do not repeat completed actions or old responses.
Omit unused fields.

Your action now: Propose scientifically useful new comparisons or refinements for later analysis.

record.narrative: No assessments are due and the voluntary validation budget is exhausted, so the final exploration focuses narrowly on gap-closing internal robustness refinements rather than a new broad program. First, I formally register the reversed version of the high-ploidy STAT3/PTEN-loss interaction (parent H280) as a claim testing attenuation. In the original high-ploidy strengthening claim, the point estimate was small but its confidence interval extended beyond the 0.10 dependency-score practical threshold in the opposite direction, leaving possible high-ploidy attenuation unresolved. With this new direction, a positive signed estimate means that the PTEN-loss contrast in high-ploidy lines is less strongly associated with STAT3 dependency than in the ploidy complement. I anticipate a positive direction because H280's point estimate favored attenuation, but I expect the result may remain unresolved because the interval was wide. Second, I add direct tests for two of the largest internal associations in the Humagne CD CRISPR library. These tests close the last major library-specific robustness gaps for the SMARCA4-loss/SMARCA2 and KEAP1-loss/NFE2L2 associations. I do not add WRN/MSI-high or STAT3/PTEN-loss Humagne-CD mean tests because their exposed-cell counts are likely below the 20-per-cell discovery requirement; broader Avana and non-Avana or KY-library tests already cover those associations where feasible. The existing active claims for adenocarcinoma-restricted SMARCA4-loss/SMARCA2 dependency and KY-library MSI-high/WRN dependency remain the highest-value pending tests, so they are not duplicated. All proposed claims remain unadjusted associations in the supplied lung-lineage CRISPR dataset and should not be interpreted as causal effects or externally transportable therapeutic predictions.

Study instructions:
Investigate diverse, scientifically meaningful comparisons and use previous
results to allocate further investigation. Broad exploration and focused follow-up are both useful
throughout the run. Assess discoveries in this supplied dataset and use independent validation when
useful. Biological interpretation and generalizability may remain uncertain.

Register comparisons, anticipated directions, and initial assessments before requesting analyses.
The controller assigns claim references. For a changed claim, propose a new comparison and link
refinements to the earlier parent claim.
Clinical log_pfs_months is natural log progression-free survival in months, fully observed without
censoring. Dependency scores are continuous; more negative values mean stronger dependency.
Research signatures are constructed standardized assays in arbitrary units. Research markers D, E,
and F are constructed binary assays with no assigned gene, pathway, or clinical role.
A mean_difference is exposed minus comparator within eligibility and subgroup. An interaction
subtracts that comparison in the subgroup complement in the same eligible population.
Use your scientific judgment to assess the size, uncertainty, and importance of each effect
and decide which conclusions the evidence supports. Explain your reasoning in the narrative.
Returned estimates and intervals are ALREADY SIGNED to the indicated hypothesis direction. Do not
multiply them by direction again. For example, raw -0.4 with direction -1 is reported as +0.4.
Discovery analyses use 95% Welch intervals and need at least 20 observations in every
comparison cell.

Each iteration has explore, analyze, appraise, and synthesize stages. Every stage may register
hypotheses for later analysis. Analyze selects up to 12 previously registered hypotheses.
Appraise assesses every new discovery result, records active/deferred/closed investigation, and may
request validation after considering those results. At most one new voluntary validation request
is allowed per iteration and ten per run. Cached requests reuse the same evidence. The evaluator
may also deliver scheduled validation during the run. Independent intervals account for the maximum
number of validation comparisons in the run. Results arrive before synthesis. Assess newly released
validation immediately in synthesis and explicitly reassess the original claim when its response
deadline appears in the context, even if you also investigate a refinement. The controller maintains
the accepted claim set from your assessments; you do not need to repeat that list. Explanations are
retained for inspection. Acceptance does not require prior independent validation.

For this task, a relative difference in outcome of 10% or greater is considered clinically significant.
Use your judgment about uncertainty and conclusions in light of this clinical significance threshold. Acceptance does not require
independent validation first. Explain your reasoning in narrative.

evidence. References H1, H2, ... identify claims; R1, R2, ... identify evidence. Copy these short

expectation

The scientific conclusion is that the supplied 2000-line lung-lineage CRISPR dataset supports four scientifically meaningful internal associations between measured predictors and CRISPR dependency scores, with strong discovery effects and independent validation for the primary estimates. Dependency scores are signed such that more negative values mean stronger dependency; for direction -1 claims, a positive signed estimate means stronger exposed dependency, while for the KEAP1-loss/NFE2L2 reverse claim H13, a positive signed estimate means weaker NFE2L2 dependency in KEAP1-loss lines.\n\nSupported core associations:\n\n1. SMARCA4 loss is associated with much stronger SMARCA2 dependency. This is the accepted claim H6 with discovery R6 signed estimate +0.784, 95% Welch interval 0.765 to 0.803, and independent validation R53 signed estimate +0.804, interval 0.775 to 0.833. The effect is far above the practical benchmark of about 0.10 dependency-score units and is reproduced in many internal strata, including screen batch, CRISPR library, matched omics QC, screen quality, ploidy strata, mutation burden, Cas9 activity, age, and co-mutation-negative strata. The robustness across strata supports internal association and not causal therapeutic targeting.\n\n2. MSI-high status is associated with much stronger WRN dependency. This is accepted claim H7 with discovery R7 signed estimate +0.790, interval 0.760 to 0.819, and validation R40 signed estimate +0.812, interval 0.765 to 0.858. The effect is extremely large relative to the dependency-scale benchmark. It is also robust across many internal strata, although prespecified effect-modification tests did not establish a reliable context-specific interaction. For example, H112 initially suggested a culture-related interaction for WRN/MSI-high, but validation reversed and the interval included zero, so it was rejected.\n\n3. KEAP1 loss is associated with weaker NFE2L2 dependency, not stronger dependency. The original direction in H8 is rejected because the raw exposed-minus-comparator difference has the opposite sign. The reverse claim H13 is accepted using discovery R8 signed estimate +0.796, interval 0.776 to 0.816, and validation R66 signed estimate +0.791, interval 0.763 to 0.820. Interpreted biologically within this dataset, KEAP1-loss cell lines have less negative, therefore weaker, NFE2L2 dependency than KEAP1-intact lines. This remains an internal association and should not be described as a causal pathway effect without external mechanistic validation.\n\n4. PTEN loss is associated with stronger STAT3 dependency. This is accepted claim H41 with discovery R25 signed estimate +0.267, interval 0.215 to 0.319, and validation R26 signed estimate +0.268, interval 0.188 to 0.348. The effect is smaller than the SMARCA2, WRN, and NFE2L2 effects but is consistently above the 0.10 practical benchmark in the primary and many stratum analyses. There is a residual possibility that high ploidy attenuates the PTEN-loss/STAT3 association because H280, which tested high-ploidy strengthening in the opposite direction, had a small opposite signed estimate and a lower signed bound extending beyond 0.10 into attenuation territory. Each iteration proceeds through explore (propose comparisons), analyze (request tests), appraise (assess the resulting discovery evidence and optionally request validation), and synthesize (assess validation and update conclusions and plans).

Study instructions:
Investigate diverse, scientifically meaningful comparisons and use previous
results to allocate further investigation. Broad exploration and focused follow-up are both useful
throughout the run. Assess discoveries in this supplied dataset and use independent validation when
useful. Biological interpretation and generalizability may remain uncertain.

Register comparisons, anticipated directions, and initial assessments before requesting analyses.
The controller assigns claim references. For a changed claim, propose a new comparison and link
refinements to the earlier parent claim.
Clinical log_pfs_months is natural log progression-free survival in months, fully observed without
censoring. Dependency scores are continuous; more negative values mean stronger dependency.
Research signatures are constructed standardized assays in arbitrary units. Research markers D, E,
and F are constructed binary assays with no assigned gene, pathway, or clinical role.
A mean_difference is exposed minus comparator within eligibility and subgroup. An interaction
subtracts that comparison in the subgroup complement in the same eligible population.
Use your scientific judgment to assess the size, uncertainty, and importance of each effect
and decide which conclusions the evidence supports. Explain your reasoning in the narrative.
Returned estimates and intervals are ALREADY SIGNED to the indicated hypothesis direction. Do not
multiply them by direction again. For example, raw -0.4 with direction -1 is reported as +0.4.
Discovery analyses use 95% Welch intervals and need at least 20 observations in every
comparison cell.

Each iteration has explore, analyze, appraise, and synthesize stages. Every stage may register
hypotheses for later analysis. Analyze selects up to 12 previously registered hypotheses.
Appraise assesses every new discovery result, records active/deferred/closed investigation, and may
request validation after considering those results. At most one new voluntary validation request
is allowed per iteration and ten per run. Cached requests reuse the same evidence. The evaluator
may also deliver scheduled validation during the run. Independent intervals account for the maximum
number of validation comparisons in the run. Results arrive before synthesis. Assess newly released
validation immediately in synthesis and explicitly reassess the original claim when its response
deadline appears in the context, even if you also investigate a refinement. The controller maintains
the accepted claim set from your assessments; you do not need to repeat that list. Explanations are
retained for inspection. Acceptance does not require prior independent validation.


You are investigating the supplied research dataset. Return one JSON object using
only this stage's response form. The service performs analyses; you choose the science.
For this task, a relative difference in outcome of 10% or greater is considered clinically significant.
Use your judgment about uncertainty and conclusions in light of this clinical significance threshold. Acceptance does not require
independent validation first. Explain your reasoning in narrative.

The ledger contains every registered claim, its current assessment, and all its available direct
evidence. References H1, H2, ... identify claims; R1, R2, ... identify evidence. Copy these short
references when needed. New proposals receive references automatically after this stage. A changed
comparison or reversed claim is a new proposal, optionally linked to an existing parent.
Proposal direction is the claim (+1 positive, -1 negative); anticipated_direction is your
expectation
of the raw exposed-minus-comparator contrast before seeing evidence (-1, 0 uncertain, +1).
initial_status is your assessment at registration. These initial judgments are recorded once.
If a proposal repeats an existing claim, the controller preserves that claim's current assessment;
use assessments to change a scientific conclusion.

For each claim in assessments_due, return one assessment with claim,
status (accept/reject/unresolved),
and investigation (active/deferred/closed). You may also reassess other claims. Omitted claims keep
their current assessment. Assess the original claim even when proposing a refinement or reversal.
By omitting evidence in an assessment, you assess all evidence displayed on that claim's card;
the controller attaches those references. To specify a subset or related evidence, provide evidence
with short R references; include the evidence listed in assessments_due for that claim.
An unchanged assessment or an investigation-only change can use evidence: [];
changing accept/reject/unresolved requires available evidence. Bookkeeping does not satisfy a due
evidence assessment.
For a refinement, parent identifies the earlier claim; omitted motivating_evidence attaches the
parent's displayed evidence. These automatic links record evidence supplied for your assessment
or refinement, not proof that you discussed or understood every result.

The controller maintains the accepted set from your assessments. Do not reconstruct it. Optional
research_notes replaces your persistent notebook; omit it to keep the existing notes. Use it for
plans or reasoning worth retaining. Latest stage narratives are also retained. All earlier numerical
evidence remains in the ledger. Do not repeat completed actions or old responses.

record.narrative:
These results complete several planned subgroup and specificity checks. The signed estimates are already oriented to each claim: for direction -1 claims, a positive estimate supports stronger, more negative dependency in the exposed group; for direction +1 KEAP1-loss/dependency_NFE2L2 claims, a positive estimate supports weaker, less negative NFE2L2 dependency in KEAP1-loss lines. I used the same conservative practical benchmark as earlier, approximately 0.10 absolute dependency-score units, because dependency scores are signed and relative differences can be unstable when comparator means are near zero.

The core associations are confirmed in their remaining important internal strata. H14 shows that SMARCA4 loss is associated with markedly stronger SMARCA2 dependency within adenocarcinoma eligibility (signed estimate 0.777; 95% lower bound 0.755), supporting acceptance and closure. I assess only H14 here to avoid duplicate canonical assessments; H62 is the same prespecified adenocarcinoma SMARCA4-loss/SMARCA2 comparison and is treated as canonicalized to this assessment. H274 confirms the MSI-high/WRN association in the KY CRISPR library (0.732; lower bound 0.675), despite a smaller exposed cell (n=32). H286 confirms SMARCA4-loss-associated SMARCA2 dependency in the Humagne CD library (0.755; lower bound 0.661), although the exposed cell is minimal at n=21, so this stratum is accepted as supportive but less stable than the larger library strata. H287 for Humagne CD KEAP1 loss and NFE2L2 dependency has only 18 exposed observations and is invalid; it is noninformative, not evidence of absence. This leaves one small Humagne-CD gap for KEAP1/NFE2L2, but the association is already strongly accepted from larger strata.

The matched-genotype and specificity analyses remain null or unsupported. EGFR amplification does not support stronger EGFR dependency in adenocarcinoma (H16/R276, estimate 0.020), and ERBB2 amplification does not support stronger ERBB2 dependency after excluding EGFR-amplified lines (H29/R277, estimate 0.001). PIK3CA mutation does not support stronger STAT3 dependency (H26/R278, signed estimate -0.014), reinforcing that the accepted STAT3 association is specific to PTEN loss rather than a broad PI3K-pathway marker. TP53 loss does not support stronger DHX9 dependency (H30/R279); the small signed estimate is opposite the claimed direction and far below the practical benchmark, so it is rejected as clinically meaningful for this hypothesis.

The interaction tests are also unsupported. ARID1A co-loss does not strengthen the SMARCA4-loss/SMARCA2 association (H33/R280, signed interaction 0.037; upper bound 0.089), and adenocarcinoma does not strengthen the KEAP1-loss/NFE2L2 association (H35/R281, signed interaction -0.012). H45 remains unresolved: the PIK3CA-mutant interaction estimate is essentially zero (0.001), but the wide interval spans -0.150 to +0.152 because of small exposed interaction cells, so a clinically meaningful strengthening cannot be ruled out, although there is no positive evidence for it. H285, the reversed high-ploidy STAT3 attenuation claim, also remains unresolved for analogous uncertainty reasons.

Overall, these new results strengthen the interpretation of four robust internal associations: SMARCA4 loss with stronger SMARCA2 dependency, MSI-high with stronger WRN dependency, KEAP1 loss with weaker NFE2L2 dependency, and PTEN loss with stronger STAT3 dependency. They also reinforce that simple matched genotype-dependency effects and many measured context interactions are null in this supplied dataset. All conclusions remain unadjusted associations within the constructed lung-lineage CRISPR dataset and are not causal or externally generalizable therapeutic claims. No validation request is possible because the voluntary validation budget is exhausted.

Study instructions:
Investigate diverse, scientifically meaningful comparisons and use previous
results to allocate further investigation. Broad exploration and focused follow-up are both useful
throughout the run. Assess discoveries in this supplied dataset and use independent validation when
useful. Biological interpretation and generalizability may remain uncertain.

Register comparisons, anticipated directions, and initial assessments before requesting analyses.
The controller assigns claim references. For a changed claim, propose a new comparison and link
refinements to the earlier parent claim.
Clinical log_pfs_months is natural log progression-free survival in months, fully observed without
censoring. Dependency scores are continuous; more negative values mean stronger dependency.
Research signatures are constructed standardized assays in arbitrary units. Research markers D, E,
and F are constructed binary assays with no assigned gene, pathway, or clinical role.
A mean_difference is exposed minus comparator within eligibility and subgroup. An interaction
subtracts that comparison in the subgroup complement in the same eligible population.
Use your scientific judgment to assess the size, uncertainty, and importance of each effect
and decide which conclusions the evidence supports. Explain your reasoning in the narrative.

multiply them by direction again. For example, raw -0.4 with direction -1 is reported as +0.4.
Discovery analyses use 95% Welch intervals and need at least 20 observations in every
comparison cell.

Each iteration has explore, analyze, appraise, and synthesize stages. Every stage may register
hypotheses for later analysis. Analyze selects up to 12 previously registered hypotheses.
Appraise assesses every new discovery result, records active/deferred/closed investigation, and may
request validation after considering those results. At most one new voluntary validation request
is allowed per iteration and ten per run. Cached requests reuse the same evidence. The evaluator
may also deliver scheduled validation during the run. Independent intervals account for the maximum
number of validation comparisons in the run. Results arrive before synthesis. Assess newly released
validation immediately in synthesis and explicitly reassess the original claim when its response
deadline appears in the context, even if you also investigate a refinement. The controller maintains
the accepted claim set from your assessments; you do not need to repeat that list. Explanations are
retained for inspection. Acceptance does not require prior independent validation.


You are investigating the supplied research dataset. Return one JSON object using
only this stage's response form. The service performs analyses; you choose the science.
For this task, a relative difference in outcome of 10% or greater is considered clinically significant.
Use your judgment about uncertainty and conclusions in light of this clinical significance threshold. Acceptance does not require
independent validation first. Explain your reasoning in narrative.

The ledger contains every registered claim, its current assessment, and all its available direct
evidence. References H1, H2, ... identify claims; R1, R2, ... identify evidence. Copy these short
references when needed. New proposals receive references automatically after this stage. A changed
comparison or reversed claim is a new proposal, optionally linked to an existing parent.

expectation
of the raw exposed-minus-comparator contrast before seeing evidence (-1, 0 uncertain, +1).
initial_status is your assessment at registration. These initial judgments are recorded once.
If a proposal repeats an existing claim, the controller preserves that claim's current assessment;
use assessments to change a scientific conclusion.

For each claim in assessments_due, return one assessment with claim,
status (accept/reject/unresolved),
and investigation (active/deferred/closed). You may also reassess other claims. Omitted claims keep
their current assessment. Assess the original claim even when proposing a refinement or reversal.
By omitting evidence in an assessment, you assess all evidence displayed on that claim's card;

For a refinement, parent identifies the earlier claim; omitted motivating_evidence attaches the
parent's displayed evidence. These automatic links record evidence supplied for your assessment
or refinement, not proof that you discussed or understood every result.

research_notes replaces your persistent notebook; omit it to keep the existing notes. Use it for
plans or reasoning worth retaining. Latest stage narratives are also retained. All earlier numerical
evidence remains in the ledger. Do not repeat completed actions or old responses.
Omit unused fields.

KEAP1 loss is associated with weaker NFE2L2 dependency, not stronger dependency. The original direction in H8 is rejected because the raw exposed-minus-comparator difference has the opposite sign. The reverse claim H13 is accepted using discovery R8 signed estimate +0.796, interval 0.776 to 0.816, and validation R66 signed estimate +0.791, interval 0.763 to 0.820. Interpreted biologically within this dataset, KEAP1-loss cell lines have less negative, therefore weaker, NFE2L2 dependency than KEAP1-intact lines. This remains an internal association and should not be described as a causal pathway effect without external mechanistic validation.\n\n4. PTEN loss is associated with stronger STAT3 dependency. This is accepted claim H41 with discovery R25 signed estimate +0.267, interval 0.215 to 0.319, and validation R26 signed estimate +0.268, interval 0.188 to 0.348. The effect is smaller than the SMARCA2, WRN, and NFE2L2 effects but is consistently above the 0.10 practical benchmark in the primary and many stratum analyses. RB1 loss with dependency_POLR2A was rejected after discovery R23 and validation R39 showed no meaningful effect.\n\n- These negative results should be read as absence of a scientifically meaningful association in this supplied dataset, not proof that such associations cannot exist in other contexts, other screens, or after adjusted modeling.\n\n- Marker and interaction screens are largely null. record.narrative: No new validation response deadlines are present and the voluntary validation budget is exhausted, so this synthesis does not modify conclusions based on newly delivered validation. The evidence remains based on discovery tests in the supplied 2000-line lung-lineage CRISPR dataset plus already completed independent validations for selected core claims. All interpretations are unadjusted internal associations, not causal effects or externally generalizable therapeutic vulnerabilities. For dependency scores I continue to use a conservative practical benchmark of roughly 0.10 absolute signed dependency-score units because dependency scores are signed and often centered near negative values, making relative percent changes unstable near zero. Accepted claims include four robust associations. First, SMARCA4 loss is associated with much stronger SMARCA2 dependency: discovery H6/R6 estimate +0.784, 95% interval 0.765 to 0.803, and validation R53 estimate +0.804, interval 0.775 to 0.833; this association is reproduced across many internal strata, including adenocarcinoma, library, QC, screen-quality, ploidy, mutation-burden, Cas9, age, and co-mutation-negative strata. Second, MSI-high status is associated with much stronger WRN dependency: discovery H7/R7 estimate +0.790, interval 0.760 to 0.819, and validation R40 estimate +0.812, interval 0.765 to 0.858; this is also reproduced broadly, including KY-library and TP53-loss strata. Third, KEAP1 loss is associated with weaker NFE2L2 dependency, opposite to the original matched genotype expectation: original H8 is rejected for the claimed direction, while reverse claim H13/R8 is accepted, estimate +0.796, interval 0.776 to 0.816, with validation R66 estimate +0.791, interval 0.763 to 0.820. Fourth, PTEN loss is associated with stronger STAT3 dependency: H41/R25 estimate +0.267, interval 0.215 to 0.319, validation R26 estimate +0.268, interval 0.188 to 0.348; this effect is smaller but still consistently exceeds the practical benchmark in primary and many subgroup analyses. Negative findings remain important. Matched genotype-dependency hypotheses are largely unsupported: KRAS mutation does not support stronger KRAS dependency, BRAF V600E does not support stronger BRAF dependency, EGFR amplification does not support stronger EGFR dependency even after independent validation, ERBB2 amplification does not support stronger ERBB2 dependency, TP53 loss does not support stronger MDM2 dependency, and several MYC-amplification hypotheses remain null. In this synthesis I formally converted many remaining unresolved but insufficiently large claims to rejected when the available 95% intervals were well below the 0.10 practical benchmark in the claimed direction, including EGFR amplification in KRAS wild-type, KRAS mutation in TP53 wild-type, several adenocarcinoma or co-mutation interaction checks, MYC/MDM2, MYC/USP7, WRN/BRCA2, DHX9/MSI, POLR2A/BRCA2, KIF18A/RB1, KRAS/STK11 in KRAS-mutant lines, Cas9-activity interaction checks, USP7/BRCA2, BRAF/NF1, EGFR amplification in double wild-type eligibility, and ARID1A co-loss within SMARCA4-loss lines. These rejections mean the supplied dataset does not support those specific meaningful associations or interactions; they do not prove absence in other datasets or adjusted models. Unresolved uncertainty is now concentrated in a few wide-interaction effects, especially EMT-related modification of the PTEN-loss/STAT3 association and high-ploidy attenuation or strengthening variants. The high-ploidy attenuation claim H285 remains unresolved because the point estimate is below the benchmark but the upper bound still allows meaningful attenuation; I closed that investigation because additional testing is unlikely to be decisive with the remaining budget. Invalid small-cell tests, including Humagne CD KEAP1/NFE2L2 and low-mutation-burden MSI strata, remain noninformative rather than negative. The most informative remaining scientific question is whether EMT-high status modifies PTEN-loss/STAT3 dependency. I registered a focused refinement of H116 using EMT >= 1.0 rather than EMT >= 0.5. H116 had a point estimate above the practical benchmark but a confidence interval crossing zero; a more extreme EMT stratum may clarify whether this is genuine effect modification or noise.
