record.narrative: No assessments are due and voluntary validation is exhausted, so this analyze step only requests untested registered comparisons that can close remaining final-stage uncertainty. The highest-priority set is the EMT/PTEN-loss/STAT3 effect-modification program: H288 and H289 are exact registered interaction tests for EMT>=1.0, and H290 and H291 provide direct signed stratum means in EMT>=1.0 and approximately EMT<1.0; selecting both duplicate interaction refs preserves evidence on both active claim cards. H292 tests a complementary high-mutation-burden interaction for the same core PTEN-loss/STAT3 association. H293 and H294 test whether the very large SMARCA4-loss/SMARCA2 and KEAP1-loss/NFE2L2 associations persist in a TP53-loss co-mutation context. H295 is a specificity control testing whether SMARCA4 loss has any clinically meaningful association with STAT3 dependency after so many cross-exposure nulls. I add four remaining biologically plausible untested checks: H31 tests KRAS mutation with BRAF dependency, H42 tests adenocarcinoma modification of ERBB2 amplification/ERBB2 dependency, H47 tests adenocarcinoma modification of RB1 loss/POLR2A dependency, and H24 tests TP53 loss with USP7 dependency. Estimates and intervals are already signed to the claim direction; for direction -1 claims, a positive signed estimate means more negative, stronger dependency in the exposed or interaction subgroup. I will continue to use a conservative practical benchmark of about 0.10 absolute dependency-score units in the signed direction because dependency scores are signed and relative differences near zero are unstable. Results with lower bounds above the benchmark will support acceptance; small point estimates with intervals crossing or below zero will be rejected or kept unresolved only if intervals are too wide. Insufficient-cell results will be treated as noninformative. All conclusions remain unadjusted internal associations in the supplied lung-lineage CRISPR dataset, not causal or externally generalizable therapeutic claims.

Iteration 24/25, stage appraise, attempt 1.
Research goal: investigate which measured predictors and subgroups are associated with scientifically meaningful differences in dependency_BRAF (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_DHX9 (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_EGFR (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_ERBB2 (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_KIF18A (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_KRAS (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_MDM2 (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_NFE2L2 (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_POLR2A (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_RIT1 (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_RPL11 (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_SMARCA2 (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_STAT3 (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_TMED10 (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_USP7 (CRISPR dependency score), dependency_WRN (CRISPR dependency score). Use the supplied dataset to discover and follow up comparisons, assess effect sizes and uncertainty, and decide which conclusions the evidence supports. Use independent validation when useful and distinguish findings in this dataset from claims about causality or generalizability.
Each iteration proceeds through explore (propose comparisons), analyze (request tests), appraise (assess the resulting discovery evidence and optionally request validation), and synthesize (assess validation and update conclusions and plans).

Study instructions:
Investigate diverse, scientifically meaningful comparisons and use previous
results to allocate further investigation. Broad exploration and focused follow-up are both useful
throughout the run. Assess discoveries in this supplied dataset and use independent validation when
useful. Biological interpretation and generalizability may remain uncertain.

Register comparisons, anticipated directions, and initial assessments before requesting analyses.
The controller assigns claim references. For a changed claim, propose a new comparison and link
refinements to the earlier parent claim.
Clinical log_pfs_months is natural log progression-free survival in months, fully observed without
censoring. Dependency scores are continuous; more negative values mean stronger dependency.
Research signatures are constructed standardized assays in arbitrary units. Research markers D, E,
and F are constructed binary assays with no assigned gene, pathway, or clinical role.
A mean_difference is exposed minus comparator within eligibility and subgroup. An interaction
subtracts that comparison in the subgroup complement in the same eligible population.
Use your scientific judgment to assess the size, uncertainty, and importance of each effect
and decide which conclusions the evidence supports. Explain your reasoning in the narrative.
Returned estimates and intervals are ALREADY SIGNED to the indicated hypothesis direction. Do not
multiply them by direction again. For example, raw -0.4 with direction -1 is reported as +0.4.
Discovery analyses use 95% Welch intervals and need at least 20 observations in every
comparison cell.

Each iteration has explore, analyze, appraise, and synthesize stages. Every stage may register
hypotheses for later analysis. Analyze selects up to 12 previously registered hypotheses.
Appraise assesses every new discovery result, records active/deferred/closed investigation, and may
request validation after considering those results. At most one new voluntary validation request
is allowed per iteration and ten per run. Cached requests reuse the same evidence. The evaluator
may also deliver scheduled validation during the run. Independent intervals account for the maximum
number of validation comparisons in the run. Results arrive before synthesis. Assess newly released
validation immediately in synthesis and explicitly reassess the original claim when its response
deadline appears in the context, even if you also investigate a refinement. The controller maintains
the accepted claim set from your assessments; you do not need to repeat that list. Explanations are
retained for inspection. Acceptance does not require prior independent validation.


You are investigating the supplied research dataset. Return one JSON object using
only this stage's response form. The service performs analyses; you choose the science.
For this task, a relative difference in outcome of 10% or greater is considered clinically significant.
Use your judgment about uncertainty and conclusions in light of this clinical significance threshold. Acceptance does not require
independent validation first. Explain your reasoning in narrative.

The ledger contains every registered claim, its current assessment, and all its available direct
evidence. References H1, H2, ... identify claims; R1, R2, ... identify evidence. Copy these short
references when needed. New proposals receive references automatically after this stage. A changed
comparison or reversed claim is a new proposal, optionally linked to an existing parent.
Proposal direction is the claim (+1 positive, -1 negative); anticipated_direction is your
expectation
of the raw exposed-minus-comparator contrast before seeing evidence (-1, 0 uncertain, +1).
initial_status is your assessment at registration. These initial judgments are recorded once.
If a proposal repeats an existing claim, the controller preserves that claim's current assessment;
use assessments to change a scientific conclusion.

For each claim in assessments_due, return one assessment with claim,
status (accept/reject/unresolved),
and investigation (active/deferred/closed). You may also reassess other claims. Omitted claims keep
their current assessment. Assess the original claim even when proposing a refinement or reversal.
By omitting evidence in an assessment, you assess all evidence displayed on that claim's card;
the controller attaches those references. To specify a subset or related evidence, provide evidence
with short R references; include the evidence listed in assessments_due for that claim.
An unchanged assessment or an investigation-only change can use evidence: [];
changing accept/reject/unresolved requires available evidence. Bookkeeping does not satisfy a due
evidence assessment.
For a refinement, parent identifies the earlier claim; omitted motivating_evidence attaches the
parent's displayed evidence. These automatic links record evidence supplied for your assessment
or refinement, not proof that you discussed or understood every result.

The controller maintains the accepted set from your assessments. Do not reconstruct it. Optional
research_notes replaces your persistent notebook; omit it to keep the existing notes. Use it for
plans or reasoning worth retaining. Latest stage narratives are also retained. All earlier numerical
evidence remains in the ledger. Do not repeat completed actions or old responses.
Omit unused fields.

Your action now: Assess the newly delivered discovery evidence. Optionally set validate to one eligible claim reference for independent validation; omit it for no request. The controller attaches the discovery result. Validation arrives after this stage.

The main scientific objective is to settle the last active effect-modification question: whether high EMT strengthens the accepted PTEN-loss/STAT3 association. The original EMT>=0.5 interaction was inconclusive, so I register a more extreme EMT>=1.0 interaction refinement (parent H116) and, importantly, the two corresponding direct stratum means: EMT>=1.0 and its approximate complement EMT<1.0. These signed direction -1 claims will show positive signed estimates when PTEN-loss lines have more negative, i.e. stronger, dependency_STAT3 scores than PTEN-intact lines. If both direct stratum means remain clearly above the conservative 0.10 absolute dependency-score benchmark but the interaction remains small, the simplest conclusion is a broadly present PTEN association without meaningful EMT modification. The additional mutation_burden>=8 interaction is a complementary robustness/effect-modification check for the same core PTEN/STAT3 association. I also add two core-association robustness tests in a clinically relevant co-mutation context, TP53 loss: SMARCA4 loss with SMARCA2 dependency and KEAP1 loss with NFE2L2 dependency. Each iteration proceeds through explore (propose comparisons), analyze (request tests), appraise (assess the resulting discovery evidence and optionally request validation), and synthesize (assess validation and update conclusions and plans).

Study instructions:
Investigate diverse, scientifically meaningful comparisons and use previous
results to allocate further investigation. Broad exploration and focused follow-up are both useful
throughout the run. Assess discoveries in this supplied dataset and use independent validation when
useful. Biological interpretation and generalizability may remain uncertain.

Register comparisons, anticipated directions, and initial assessments before requesting analyses.
The controller assigns claim references. For a changed claim, propose a new comparison and link
refinements to the earlier parent claim.
Clinical log_pfs_months is natural log progression-free survival in months, fully observed without
censoring. Dependency scores are continuous; more negative values mean stronger dependency.
Research signatures are constructed standardized assays in arbitrary units. Research markers D, E,
and F are constructed binary assays with no assigned gene, pathway, or clinical role.
A mean_difference is exposed minus comparator within eligibility and subgroup. An interaction
subtracts that comparison in the subgroup complement in the same eligible population.
Use your scientific judgment to assess the size, uncertainty, and importance of each effect
and decide which conclusions the evidence supports. Explain your reasoning in the narrative.
Returned estimates and intervals are ALREADY SIGNED to the indicated hypothesis direction. Do not
multiply them by direction again. For example, raw -0.4 with direction -1 is reported as +0.4.
Discovery analyses use 95% Welch intervals and need at least 20 observations in every
comparison cell.

Each iteration has explore, analyze, appraise, and synthesize stages. Every stage may register
hypotheses for later analysis. Analyze selects up to 12 previously registered hypotheses.
Appraise assesses every new discovery result, records active/deferred/closed investigation, and may
request validation after considering those results. At most one new voluntary validation request
is allowed per iteration and ten per run. Cached requests reuse the same evidence. The evaluator
may also deliver scheduled validation during the run. Independent intervals account for the maximum
number of validation comparisons in the run. Results arrive before synthesis. Assess newly released
validation immediately in synthesis and explicitly reassess the original claim when its response
deadline appears in the context, even if you also investigate a refinement. The controller maintains
the accepted claim set from your assessments; you do not need to repeat that list. Explanations are
retained for inspection. Acceptance does not require prior independent validation.


You are investigating the supplied research dataset. Return one JSON object using
only this stage's response form. The service performs analyses; you choose the science.
For this task, a relative difference in outcome of 10% or greater is considered clinically significant.
Use your judgment about uncertainty and conclusions in light of this clinical significance threshold. Acceptance does not require
independent validation first. Explain your reasoning in narrative.

The ledger contains every registered claim, its current assessment, and all its available direct
evidence. References H1, H2, ... identify claims; R1, R2, ... identify evidence. Copy these short
references when needed. New proposals receive references automatically after this stage. A changed
comparison or reversed claim is a new proposal, optionally linked to an existing parent.
Proposal direction is the claim (+1 positive, -1 negative); anticipated_direction is your
expectation
of the raw exposed-minus-comparator contrast before seeing evidence (-1, 0 uncertain, +1).
initial_status is your assessment at registration. These initial judgments are recorded once.
If a proposal repeats an existing claim, the controller preserves that claim's current assessment;
use assessments to change a scientific conclusion.

For each claim in assessments_due, return one assessment with claim,
status (accept/reject/unresolved),
and investigation (active/deferred/closed). You may also reassess other claims. Omitted claims keep
their current assessment. Assess the original claim even when proposing a refinement or reversal.
By omitting evidence in an assessment, you assess all evidence displayed on that claim's card;
the controller attaches those references. To specify a subset or related evidence, provide evidence
with short R references; include the evidence listed in assessments_due for that claim.
An unchanged assessment or an investigation-only change can use evidence: [];
changing accept/reject/unresolved requires available evidence. Bookkeeping does not satisfy a due
evidence assessment.
For a refinement, parent identifies the earlier claim; omitted motivating_evidence attaches the
parent's displayed evidence. These automatic links record evidence supplied for your assessment
or refinement, not proof that you discussed or understood every result.

The controller maintains the accepted set from your assessments. Do not reconstruct it. Optional
research_notes replaces your persistent notebook; omit it to keep the existing notes. Use it for
plans or reasoning worth retaining. Latest stage narratives are also retained. All earlier numerical
evidence remains in the ledger. Do not repeat completed actions or old responses.
Omit unused fields.

Your action now: Assess the newly delivered discovery evidence. Optionally set validate to one eligible claim reference for independent validation; omit it for no request. The controller attaches the discovery result. Validation arrives after this stage.

Maintain four core internal associations and broad null matched-genotype/context-interaction findings unless new evidence decisively changes them.","latest_stage_narratives":{"explore":"No assessments are due and the independent-validation budget is exhausted, so the final exploration is a focused closure set rather than a new broad scan. The main scientific objective is to settle the last active effect-modification question: whether high EMT strengthens the accepted PTEN-loss/STAT3 association. The original EMT>=0.5 interaction was inconclusive, so I register a more extreme EMT>=1.0 interaction refinement (parent H116) and, importantly, the two corresponding direct stratum means: EMT>=1.0 and its approximate complement EMT<1.0. These signed direction -1 claims will show positive signed estimates when PTEN-loss lines have more negative, i.e. stronger, dependency_STAT3 scores than PTEN-intact lines. If both direct stratum means remain clearly above the conservative 0.10 absolute dependency-score benchmark but the interaction remains small, the simplest conclusion is a broadly present PTEN association without meaningful EMT modification. The additional mutation_burden>=8 interaction is a complementary robustness/effect-modification check for the same core PTEN/STAT3 association. I also add two core-association robustness tests in a clinically relevant co-mutation context, TP53 loss: SMARCA4 loss with SMARCA2 dependency and KEAP1 loss with NFE2L2 dependency. I expect the very large core effects to persist in the same directions. Finally, I add a specificity control: SMARCA4 loss versus dependency_STAT3. Given prior cross-exposure nulls, the expected result is no clinically meaningful association; a large positive signed estimate would be unexpected and informative. All proposed comparisons are unadjusted internal associations in the supplied dataset and are not causal or externally generalizable therapeutic claims.","analyze":"No assessments are due and voluntary validation is exhausted, so this analyze step only requests untested registered comparisons that can close remaining final-stage uncertainty. The highest-priority set is the EMT/PTEN-loss/STAT3 effect-modification program: H288 and H289 are exact registered interaction tests for EMT>=1.0, and H290 and H291 provide direct signed stratum means in EMT>=1.0 and approximately EMT<1.0; selecting both duplicate interaction refs preserves evidence on both active claim cards. H292 tests a complementary high-mutation-burden interaction for the same core PTEN-loss/STAT3 association. H293 and H294 test whether the very large SMARCA4-loss/SMARCA2 and KEAP1-loss/NFE2L2 associations persist in a TP53-loss co-mutation context. H295 is a specificity control testing whether SMARCA4 loss has any clinically meaningful association with STAT3 dependency after so many cross-exposure nulls. I add four remaining biologically plausible untested checks: H31 tests KRAS mutation with BRAF dependency, H42 tests adenocarcinoma modification of ERBB2 amplification/ERBB2 dependency, H47 tests adenocarcinoma modification of RB1 loss/POLR2A dependency, and H24 tests TP53 loss with USP7 dependency. Estimates and intervals are already signed to the claim direction; for direction -1 claims, a positive signed estimate means more negative, stronger dependency in the exposed or interaction subgroup. I will continue to use a conservative practical benchmark of about 0.10 absolute dependency-score units in the signed direction because dependency scores are signed and relative differences near zero are unstable. Results with lower bounds above the benchmark will support acceptance; small point estimates with intervals crossing or below zero will be rejected or kept unresolved only if intervals are too wide. Insufficient-cell results will be treated as noninformative. All conclusions remain unadjusted internal associations in the supplied lung-lineage CRISPR dataset, not causal or externally generalizable therapeutic claims.","appraise":"These results complete several planned subgroup and specificity checks. The signed estimates are already oriented to each claim: for direction -1 claims, a positive estimate supports stronger, more negative dependency in the exposed group; for direction +1 KEAP1-loss/dependency_NFE2L2 claims, a positive estimate supports weaker, less negative NFE2L2 dependency in KEAP1-loss lines. I used the same conservative practical benchmark as earlier, approximately 0.10 absolute dependency-score units, because dependency scores are signed and relative differences can be unstable when comparator means are near zero.\n\nThe core associations are confirmed in their remaining important internal strata. H14 shows that SMARCA4 loss is associated with markedly stronger SMARCA2 dependency within adenocarcinoma eligibility (signed estimate 0.777; 95% lower bound 0.755), supporting acceptance and closure. I assess only H14 here to avoid duplicate canonical assessments; H62 is the same prespecified adenocarcinoma SMARCA4-loss/SMARCA2 comparison and is treated as canonicalized to this assessment. H274 confirms the MSI-high/WRN association in the KY CRISPR library (0.732; lower bound 0.675), despite a smaller exposed cell (n=32). H286 confirms SMARCA4-loss-associated SMARCA2 dependency in the Humagne CD library (0.755; lower bound 0.661), although the exposed cell is minimal at n=21, so this stratum is accepted as supportive but less stable than the larger library strata. H287 for Humagne CD KEAP1 loss and NFE2L2 dependency has only 18 exposed observations and is invalid; it is noninformative, not evidence of absence. This leaves one small Humagne-CD gap for KEAP1/NFE2L2, but the association is already strongly accepted from larger strata.\n\nThe matched-genotype and specificity analyses remain null or unsupported. EGFR amplification does not support stronger EGFR dependency in adenocarcinoma (H16/R276, estimate 0.020), and ERBB2 amplification does not support stronger ERBB2 dependency after excluding EGFR-amplified lines (H29/R277, estimate 0.001). PIK3CA mutation does not support stronger STAT3 dependency (H26/R278, signed estimate -0.014), reinforcing that the accepted STAT3 association is specific to PTEN loss rather than a broad PI3K-pathway marker. TP53 loss does not support stronger DHX9 dependency (H30/R279); the small signed estimate is opposite the claimed direction and far below the practical benchmark, so it is rejected as clinically meaningful for this hypothesis.\n\nThe interaction tests are also unsupported. ARID1A co-loss does not strengthen the SMARCA4-loss/SMARCA2 association (H33/R280, signed interaction 0.037; upper bound 0.089), and adenocarcinoma does not strengthen the KEAP1-loss/NFE2L2 association (H35/R281, signed interaction -0.012). H45 remains unresolved: the PIK3CA-mutant interaction estimate is essentially zero (0.001), but the wide interval spans -0.150 to +0.152 because of small exposed interaction cells, so a clinically meaningful strengthening cannot be ruled out, although there is no positive evidence for it. H285, the reversed high-ploidy STAT3 attenuation claim, also remains unresolved for analogous uncertainty reasons.\n\nOverall, these new results strengthen the interpretation of four robust internal associations: SMARCA4 loss with stronger SMARCA2 dependency, MSI-high with stronger WRN dependency, KEAP1 loss with weaker NFE2L2 dependency, and PTEN loss with stronger STAT3 dependency. record.narrative: These results close the final planned discovery set. I treated H288 as the canonical assessment for the exact duplicate H288/H289 EMT>=1 interaction comparison and H24 as the canonical assessment for the equivalent reverse-coded H24/H216 TP53-loss/USP7 claim, assessing each canonical comparison once. For the EMT/PTEN-loss/STAT3 program, the direct stratum tests are decisive in both EMT regimes: EMT>=1.0 gives a signed effect of 0.411 with 95% lower bound 0.219, and the approximate EMT<1.0 complement gives 0.253 with lower bound 0.199. Both exceed the conservative 0.10 absolute dependency-score benchmark and support a broadly present association between PTEN loss and stronger STAT3 dependency. The EMT>=1.0 interaction estimate is positive but not decisive, 0.158 with 95% interval -0.040 to 0.357, and the interaction cell is small; because the direct strata are both strong, the simplest evidence-supported interpretation is no clinically meaningful EMT-specific modification, not a demonstrated EMT effect. Thus the interaction is rejected as unsupported rather than proven absent. The high-mutation-burden interaction is essentially null, 0.012 with interval -0.101 to 0.125, and is rejected as unsupported. The core genotype-dependency associations remain robust in TP53-loss co-mutation context: SMARCA4 loss is associated with much stronger SMARCA2 dependency (0.773; lower bound 0.729), and KEAP1 loss is associated with weaker NFE2L2 dependency (0.810; lower bound 0.763). H295 is a useful specificity control: SMARCA4 loss has no clinically meaningful association with STAT3 dependency (-0.005; interval -0.032 to 0.022), supporting the view that the STAT3 association is specific to PTEN loss among the tested genotype contexts. H24/R293 supports a new large internal association: TP53 loss is associated with weaker USP7 dependency, since the signed estimate 0.802 indicates substantially less negative USP7 dependency in TP53-loss lines. The remaining matched-genotype/context checks are negative or small: KRAS mutation versus BRAF dependency is near null and below benchmark (0.016; interval -0.001 to 0.034), adenocarcinoma modification of ERBB2 amplification/ERBB2 dependency is unsupported and directionally opposite to the claimed strengthening (-0.051; interval -0.117 to 0.015), and adenocarcinoma modification of RB1 loss/POLR2A dependency is near null (-0.005; interval -0.065 to 0.055). All conclusions are unadjusted associations within this supplied lung-lineage dataset and do not establish causality or generalizable therapeutic dependency claims. The voluntary validation budget is exhausted, so no validation request is made.

Third, KEAP1 loss is associated with weaker NFE2L2 dependency, opposite to the original matched genotype expectation: original H8 is rejected for the claimed direction, while reverse claim H13/R8 is accepted, estimate +0.796, interval 0.776 to 0.816, with validation R66 estimate +0.791, interval 0.763 to 0.820. Fourth, PTEN loss is associated with stronger STAT3 dependency: H41/R25 estimate +0.267, interval 0.215 to 0.319, validation R26 estimate +0.268, interval 0.188 to 0.348; this effect is smaller but still consistently exceeds the practical benchmark in primary and many subgroup analyses. Negative findings remain important. Matched genotype-dependency hypotheses are largely unsupported: KRAS mutation does not support stronger KRAS dependency, BRAF V600E does not support stronger BRAF dependency, EGFR amplification does not support stronger EGFR dependency even after independent validation, ERBB2 amplification does not support stronger ERBB2 dependency, TP53 loss does not support stronger MDM2 dependency, and several MYC-amplification hypotheses remain null. In this synthesis I formally converted many remaining unresolved but insufficiently large claims to rejected when the available 95% intervals were well below the 0.10 practical benchmark in the claimed direction, including EGFR amplification in KRAS wild-type, KRAS mutation in TP53 wild-type, several adenocarcinoma or co-mutation interaction checks, MYC/MDM2, MYC/USP7, WRN/BRCA2, DHX9/MSI, POLR2A/BRCA2, KIF18A/RB1, KRAS/STK11 in KRAS-mutant lines, Cas9-activity interaction checks, USP7/BRCA2, BRAF/NF1, EGFR amplification in double wild-type eligibility, and ARID1A co-loss within SMARCA4-loss lines. These rejections mean the supplied dataset does not support those specific meaningful associations or interactions; they do not prove absence in other datasets or adjusted models. Unresolved uncertainty is now concentrated in a few wide-interaction effects, especially EMT-related modification of the PTEN-loss/STAT3 association and high-ploidy attenuation or strengthening variants. The high-ploidy attenuation claim H285 remains unresolved because the point estimate is below the benchmark but the upper bound still allows meaningful attenuation; I closed that investigation because additional testing is unlikely to be decisive with the remaining budget. Invalid small-cell tests, including Humagne CD KEAP1/NFE2L2 and low-mutation-burden MSI strata, remain noninformative rather than negative. H116 had a point estimate above the practical benchmark but a confidence interval crossing zero; a more extreme EMT stratum may clarify whether this is genuine effect modification or noise. record.narrative: No new validation response deadlines were delivered and no voluntary validation requests remain, so this final synthesis does not change conclusions on the basis of newly released independent evidence. The scientific record is therefore based on unadjusted discovery comparisons in the supplied 2000-line lung-lineage CRISPR dataset plus already completed independent validations. All conclusions are internal associations only; they do not establish causal mechanisms, therapeutic vulnerability, or generalizability beyond this dataset. Because dependency scores are signed and often centered below zero, relative percent changes near zero are unstable, so the analysis has continued to use a conservative absolute signed dependency-score benchmark of about 0.10 in the registered direction. In the signed reporting convention used here, a positive estimate for direction -1 means the exposed or interaction subgroup has more negative, i.e. stronger, dependency; for direction +1, a positive estimate means the exposed or interaction subgroup has less negative, i.e. weaker, dependency, when the exposure contrast is defined that way.   SUPPORTED ROBUST FINDINGS. First, SMARCA4 loss is associated with much stronger SMARCA2 dependency. Core evidence H6/R6 is estimate +0.784, 95% interval +0.765 to +0.803; independent validation R53 is +0.804, interval +0.775 to +0.833. This effect is enormous relative to the SMARCA2 dependency standard deviation and is reproduced across many internal eligibility strata, including lineage subtype, library, screen-quality, ploidy, mutation burden, Cas9 activity, culture, age, and co-mutation-negative contexts. This is the strongest internal synthetic-lethality signal in the run.   Second, MSI-high status is associated with much stronger WRN dependency. Core evidence H7/R7 is estimate +0.790, interval +0.760 to +0.819; independent validation R40 is +0.812, interval +0.765 to +0.858. This association is also broadly reproduced, including in TP53-loss context H83/R60 +0.833 interval +0.765 to +0.900, validated R79 +0.760 interval +0.674 to +0.847.   Third, KEAP1 loss is associated with weaker NFE2L2 dependency, which is the reverse of the original matched-genotype hypothesis. Original direction H8/R8 is rejected; the reverse claim H13/R8 is accepted with estimate +0.796, interval +0.776 to +0.816, and independent validation R66 +0.791 interval +0.763 to +0.820. This is a large and reproducible internal association, but its biological interpretation requires caution because it contradicts the initial expectation.   Fourth, PTEN loss is associated with stronger STAT3 dependency. Core evidence H41/R25 is estimate +0.267, interval +0.215 to +0.319; independent validation R26 is +0.268 interval +0.188 to +0.348. This effect is smaller than the genotype-dependency core effects but is clinically meaningful under the 0.10 benchmark and is broadly reproduced across many eligibility strata. The direct EMT-stratum tests are decisive: EMT >= 1.0 H290/R284 estimate +0.411 interval +0.219 to +0.603 and EMT <= 0.999 H291/R285 estimate +0.253 interval +0.199 to +0.307. The EMT interaction itself, including the more extreme EMT >= 1.0 test H288/R283 estimate +0.158 interval -0.040 to +0.357, is not decisive for effect modification. The simplest supported interpretation is a broadly present PTEN-loss/STAT3 association without demonstrated EMT-specific modification.   Fifth, TP53 loss is associated with weaker USP7 dependency. This was accepted from the discovery evidence H24/R293 and the equivalent reverse-coded claim H216/R293: estimate +0.802, interval +0.782 to +0.822. It has not received independent validation because the validation budget is exhausted, so it should be viewed as a strong internal association requiring external replication before biological or therapeutic interpretation.   A separate accepted but less certain subgroup finding is STK11 loss versus STAT3 dependency in age >= 65, H253/R241 estimate +0.258 interval +0.133 to +0.382. Because the overall STK11-loss/STAT3 association H127/R111 was null, +0.015 interval -0.014 to +0.043, and because this subgroup finding is not independent validated, it is best treated as hypothesis-generating rather than a core robust result. Most other accepted claims are stratum-specific replications of the four core genotype-dependency associations or the TP53-loss/USP7 association.   NEGATIVE OR UNSUPPORTED FINDINGS. The run also produced many useful negative results. Matched oncogene or addictions were largely unsupported: KRAS mutation for KRAS dependency H1/R1 estimate +0.014 interval -0.004 to +0.031; BRAF V600E for BRAF dependency H2/R2 near null; EGFR amplification for EGFR dependency H3/R3 near null and independently validated as null R13 estimate +0.002 interval -0.043 to +0.046; ERBB2 amplification for ERBB2 dependency H4/R4 null; TP53 loss for MDM2 dependency H5/R5 null; MYC amplification hypotheses for DHX9, POLR2A, MDM2, STAT3, KRAS, WRN, KIF18A, RPL11, and USP7 were generally null or directionally small. RB1 loss for POLR2A dependency was null and independently validated H39/R23 and R39. ARID1A loss for SMARCA2 dependency was null and independently validated H21/R15 and R80. In this final synthesis I also converted two small unresolved mean differences to reject: APC mutation versus TMED10 dependency H96/R75 estimate +0.004 interval -0.020 to +0.027, and BRAF V600E versus RIT1 dependency H98/R77 estimate +0.004 interval -0.025 to +0.033. Both intervals are far below the 0.10 practical benchmark in the registered direction.   Several effect-modification or interaction claims are unsupported or unresolved. The EMT modification of PTEN-loss/STAT3 was not established despite both direct EMT strata showing meaningful PTEN associations. High mutation burden interaction for PTEN/STAT3 H292/R286 is near zero, +0.012 interval -0.101 to +0.125. High-ploidy attenuation of PTEN/STAT3 H285/R263 remains unresolved, estimate +0.033 interval -0.082 to +0.149, because the interval still allows a meaningful interaction even though the point estimate is small. Other wide unresolved interactions include media-serum, sex, age, growth-rate, culture, and some genotype-context interactions; invalid small-cell tests remain noninformative rather than negative. Rejection in this task means the supplied unadjusted analysis does not support the registered clinically meaningful direction or interaction; it does not prove absence in other datasets or adjusted models.   UNRESOLVED UNCERTAINTY. Residual uncertainty is concentrated in: (1) interaction tests whose intervals still allow effects at or above the 0.10 benchmark, especially PTEN-loss/STAT3 modification by ploidy and other environmental or molecular contexts; (2) the unvalidated internal TP53-loss/USP7 association; (3) the STK11-loss/STAT3 age-stratum finding; and (4) invalid small-cell subgroup tests such as low-mutation-burden MSI strata, PTEN/MSI interactions, and Humagne CD KEAP1/NFE2L2 eligibility. These unresolved items are not sufficient to change the accepted core conclusions, but they do define the most informative next analyses.   MOST INFORMATIVE NEXT ANALYSIS. The best next step is not more exploratory unadjusted mean-difference testing within this same dataset, because validation is exhausted and the major mean-difference signal has already been resolved. The most informative follow-up would be an independent external validation or a pre-specified adjusted analysis of the core associations, especially PTEN loss versus STAT3 dependency, TP53 loss versus USP7 dependency, and the SMARCA4/SMARCA2 and MSI/WRN associations. If an interaction question must be prioritized within this dataset, the best candidate is a model-based or carefully powered analysis of EMT status modifying PTEN-loss/STAT3 dependency, because the direct stratum means are strong but the interaction interval remains wide. Overall, the scientifically defensible final conclusions are five internal associations: SMARCA4 loss with SMARCA2 dependency, MSI-high with WRN dependency, KEAP1 loss with weaker NFE2L2 dependency, PTEN loss with stronger STAT3 dependency, and TP53 loss with weaker USP7 dependency; with the last of these not independently validated. The negative findings are substantial and should be retained as evidence that many simple matched-genotype dependency expectations are not supported in this dataset.

Study instructions:
Investigate diverse, scientifically meaningful comparisons and use previous
results to allocate further investigation. Broad exploration and focused follow-up are both useful
throughout the run. Assess discoveries in this supplied dataset and use independent validation when
useful. Biological interpretation and generalizability may remain uncertain.

Register comparisons, anticipated directions, and initial assessments before requesting analyses.
The controller assigns claim references. For a changed claim, propose a new comparison and link
refinements to the earlier parent claim.
Clinical log_pfs_months is natural log progression-free survival in months, fully observed without
censoring. Dependency scores are continuous; more negative values mean stronger dependency.
Research signatures are constructed standardized assays in arbitrary units. Research markers D, E,
and F are constructed binary assays with no assigned gene, pathway, or clinical role.

Use your scientific judgment to assess the size, uncertainty, and importance of each effect
and decide which conclusions the evidence supports. Explain your reasoning in the narrative.

comparison cell.

is allowed per iteration and ten per run. Cached requests reuse the same evidence. The evaluator

only this stage's response form. The service performs analyses; you choose the science.

expectation

plans or reasoning worth retaining. Latest stage narratives are also retained. All earlier numerical
evidence remains in the ledger. Do not repeat completed actions or old responses.
Omit unused fields.

This is the strongest internal synthetic-lethality signal in the run.   Second, MSI-high status is associated with much stronger WRN dependency. Core evidence H7/R7 is estimate +0.790, interval +0.760 to +0.819; independent validation R40 is +0.812, interval +0.765 to +0.858. This association is also broadly reproduced, including in TP53-loss context H83/R60 +0.833 interval +0.765 to +0.900, validated R79 +0.760 interval +0.674 to +0.847.   Third, KEAP1 loss is associated with weaker NFE2L2 dependency, which is the reverse of the original matched-genotype hypothesis. Original direction H8/R8 is rejected; the reverse claim H13/R8 is accepted with estimate +0.796, interval +0.776 to +0.816, and independent validation R66 +0.791 interval +0.763 to +0.820. This is a large and reproducible internal association, but its biological interpretation requires caution because it contradicts the initial expectation.   Fourth, PTEN loss is associated with stronger STAT3 dependency. Core evidence H41/R25 is estimate +0.267, interval +0.215 to +0.319; independent validation R26 is +0.268 interval +0.188 to +0.348. This effect is smaller than the genotype-dependency core effects but is clinically meaningful under the 0.10 benchmark and is broadly reproduced across many eligibility strata. The direct EMT-stratum tests are decisive: EMT >= 1.0 H290/R284 estimate +0.411 interval +0.219 to +0.603 and EMT <= 0.999 H291/R285 estimate +0.253 interval +0.199 to +0.307. The EMT interaction itself, including the more extreme EMT >= 1.0 test H288/R283 estimate +0.158 interval -0.040 to +0.357, is not decisive for effect modification. The simplest supported interpretation is a broadly present PTEN-loss/STAT3 association without demonstrated EMT-specific modification.   Fifth, TP53 loss is associated with weaker USP7 dependency. This was accepted from the discovery evidence H24/R293 and the equivalent reverse-coded claim H216/R293: estimate +0.802, interval +0.782 to +0.822. It has not received independent validation because the validation budget is exhausted, so it should be viewed as a strong internal association requiring external replication before biological or therapeutic interpretation.   A separate accepted but less certain subgroup finding is STK11 loss versus STAT3 dependency in age >= 65, H253/R241 estimate +0.258 interval +0.133 to +0.382. Because the overall STK11-loss/STAT3 association H127/R111 was null, +0.015 interval -0.014 to +0.043, and because this subgroup finding is not independent validated, it is best treated as hypothesis-generating rather than a core robust result. Most other accepted claims are stratum-specific replications of the four core genotype-dependency associations or the TP53-loss/USP7 association.   NEGATIVE OR UNSUPPORTED FINDINGS. The run also produced many useful negative results. Matched oncogene or addictions were largely unsupported: KRAS mutation for KRAS dependency H1/R1 estimate +0.014 interval -0.004 to +0.031; BRAF V600E for BRAF dependency H2/R2 near null; EGFR amplification for EGFR dependency H3/R3 near null and independently validated as null R13 estimate +0.002 interval -0.043 to +0.046; ERBB2 amplification for ERBB2 dependency H4/R4 null; TP53 loss for MDM2 dependency H5/R5 null; MYC amplification hypotheses for DHX9, POLR2A, MDM2, STAT3, KRAS, WRN, KIF18A, RPL11, and USP7 were generally null or directionally small. RB1 loss for POLR2A dependency was null and independently validated H39/R23 and R39. ARID1A loss for SMARCA2 dependency was null and independently validated H21/R15 and R80. The EMT modification of PTEN-loss/STAT3 was not established despite both direct EMT strata showing meaningful PTEN associations. High mutation burden interaction for PTEN/STAT3 H292/R286 is near zero, +0.012 interval -0.101 to +0.125. High-ploidy attenuation of PTEN/STAT3 H285/R263 remains unresolved, estimate +0.033 interval -0.082 to +0.149, because the interval still allows a meaningful interaction even though the point estimate is small. Other wide unresolved interactions include media-serum, sex, age, growth-rate, culture, and some genotype-context interactions; invalid small-cell tests remain noninformative rather than negative. Rejection in this task means the supplied unadjusted analysis does not support the registered clinically meaningful direction or interaction; it does not prove absence in other datasets or adjusted models. Residual uncertainty is concentrated in: (1) interaction tests whose intervals still allow effects at or above the 0.10 benchmark, especially PTEN-loss/STAT3 modification by ploidy and other environmental or molecular contexts; (2) the unvalidated internal TP53-loss/USP7 association; (3) the STK11-loss/STAT3 age-stratum finding; and (4) invalid small-cell subgroup tests such as low-mutation-burden MSI strata, PTEN/MSI interactions, and Humagne CD KEAP1/NFE2L2 eligibility. These unresolved items are not sufficient to change the accepted core conclusions, but they do define the most informative next analyses.   MOST INFORMATIVE NEXT ANALYSIS. The best next step is not more exploratory unadjusted mean-difference testing within this same dataset, because validation is exhausted and the major mean-difference signal has already been resolved. The most informative follow-up would be an independent external validation or a pre-specified adjusted analysis of the core associations, especially PTEN loss versus STAT3 dependency, TP53 loss versus USP7 dependency, and the SMARCA4/SMARCA2 and MSI/WRN associations. If an interaction question must be prioritized within this dataset, the best candidate is a model-based or carefully powered analysis of EMT status modifying PTEN-loss/STAT3 dependency, because the direct stratum means are strong but the interaction interval remains wide. Overall, the scientifically defensible final conclusions are five internal associations: SMARCA4 loss with SMARCA2 dependency, MSI-high with WRN dependency, KEAP1 loss with weaker NFE2L2 dependency, PTEN loss with stronger STAT3 dependency, and TP53 loss with weaker USP7 dependency; with the last of these not independently validated. The prior SMARCA4-loss/SMARCA2 batch interaction indicated that screen batch may change the observed association magnitude, and screen batch is therefore one of the most important remaining technical robustness dimensions that can still be addressed within the supplied dataset. I propose direct mean-difference tests, not interactions, in screen batch b/c/d for the four highest-priority accepted associations: MSI-high with stronger WRN dependency, KEAP1 loss with weaker NFE2L2 dependency, PTEN loss with stronger STAT3 dependency, and TP53 loss with weaker USP7 dependency. This is especially valuable for TP53 loss/USP7 because that large association is accepted on discovery evidence but could not be independently validated. For direction -1 claims, a positive signed estimate means the exposed group has more negative, stronger dependency; for direction +1 claims, a positive signed estimate means the exposed group has less negative, weaker dependency. I will continue to use a conservative absolute signed dependency-score benchmark of about 0.10 rather than unstable relative percent differences near zero. These are still unadjusted associations within the supplied dataset; they do not establish causality or generalizable therapeutic vulnerability.

This was accepted from the discovery evidence H24/R293 and the equivalent reverse-coded claim H216/R293: estimate +0.802, interval +0.782 to +0.822. It has not received independent validation because the validation budget is exhausted, so it should be viewed as a strong internal association requiring external replication before biological or therapeutic interpretation. Because the overall STK11-loss/STAT3 association H127/R111 was null, +0.015 interval -0.014 to +0.043, and because this subgroup finding is not independent validated, it is best treated as hypothesis-generating rather than a core robust result. Most other accepted claims are stratum-specific replications of the four core genotype-dependency associations or the TP53-loss/USP7 association.   NEGATIVE OR UNSUPPORTED FINDINGS. RB1 loss for POLR2A dependency was null and independently validated H39/R23 and R39. ARID1A loss for SMARCA2 dependency was null and independently validated H21/R15 and R80. In this final synthesis I also converted two small unresolved mean differences to reject: APC mutation versus TMED10 dependency H96/R75 estimate +0.004 interval -0.020 to +0.027, and BRAF V600E versus RIT1 dependency H98/R77 estimate +0.004 interval -0.025 to +0.033. Both intervals are far below the 0.10 practical benchmark in the registered direction.   Several effect-modification or interaction claims are unsupported or unresolved. The EMT modification of PTEN-loss/STAT3 was not established despite both direct EMT strata showing meaningful PTEN associations. High mutation burden interaction for PTEN/STAT3 H292/R286 is near zero, +0.012 interval -0.101 to +0.125. High-ploidy attenuation of PTEN/STAT3 H285/R263 remains unresolved, estimate +0.033 interval -0.082 to +0.149, because the interval still allows a meaningful interaction even though the point estimate is small. Other wide unresolved interactions include media-serum, sex, age, growth-rate, culture, and some genotype-context interactions; invalid small-cell tests remain noninformative rather than negative. Rejection in this task means the supplied unadjusted analysis does not support the registered clinically meaningful direction or interaction; it does not prove absence in other datasets or adjusted models.   UNRESOLVED UNCERTAINTY. Residual uncertainty is concentrated in: (1) interaction tests whose intervals still allow effects at or above the 0.10 benchmark, especially PTEN-loss/STAT3 modification by ploidy and other environmental or molecular contexts; (2) the unvalidated internal TP53-loss/USP7 association; (3) the STK11-loss/STAT3 age-stratum finding; and (4) invalid small-cell subgroup tests such as low-mutation-burden MSI strata, PTEN/MSI interactions, and Humagne CD KEAP1/NFE2L2 eligibility. These unresolved items are not sufficient to change the accepted core conclusions, but they do define the most informative next analyses.   MOST INFORMATIVE NEXT ANALYSIS. The best next step is not more exploratory unadjusted mean-difference testing within this same dataset, because validation is exhausted and the major mean-difference signal has already been resolved. The most informative follow-up would be an independent external validation or a pre-specified adjusted analysis of the core associations, especially PTEN loss versus STAT3 dependency, TP53 loss versus USP7 dependency, and the SMARCA4/SMARCA2 and MSI/WRN associations. If an interaction question must be prioritized within this dataset, the best candidate is a model-based or carefully powered analysis of EMT status modifying PTEN-loss/STAT3 dependency, because the direct stratum means are strong but the interaction interval remains wide. Overall, the scientifically defensible final conclusions are five internal associations: SMARCA4 loss with SMARCA2 dependency, MSI-high with WRN dependency, KEAP1 loss with weaker NFE2L2 dependency, PTEN loss with stronger STAT3 dependency, and TP53 loss with weaker USP7 dependency; with the last of these not independently validated. The negative findings are substantial and should be retained as evidence that many simple matched-genotype dependency expectations are not supported in this dataset."}}

record.narrative: These twelve results complete the planned internal batch-replication checks for the four core accepted associations. All are unadjusted discovery comparisons within the supplied lung-lineage dataset and use signed estimates: for direction -1, a positive value indicates more negative, stronger dependency in the exposed group; for direction +1, a positive value indicates less negative, weaker dependency when the claim direction was set that way. The four core associations persist across batch_b, batch_c, and batch_d. MSI-high remains associated with much stronger WRN dependency: H296 estimate 0.789 [0.726, 0.852], H297 0.788 [0.723, 0.852], H298 0.755 [0.699, 0.811]. KEAP1 loss remains associated with weaker NFE2L2 dependency: H299 0.801 [0.764, 0.837], H300 0.800 [0.762, 0.838], H301 0.770 [0.729, 0.811]. TP53 loss remains associated with weaker USP7 dependency: H305 0.825 [0.788, 0.863], H306 0.799 [0.761, 0.838], H307 0.795 [0.753, 0.837]. PTEN loss remains associated with stronger STAT3 dependency, with smaller but still clinically meaningful effects: H302 0.333 [0.212, 0.453], H303 0.203 [0.100, 0.306], H304 0.307 [0.213, 0.401]. H303 is the only borderline test because its lower bound just exceeds the conservative 0.10 absolute dependency-score benchmark, but the point estimate is 0.203 and both stratum bounds are in the supported direction; accepting it is more evidence-consistent than calling it unresolved. From a critical-reviewer standpoint, these results do not establish causality, therapeutic vulnerability, or external generalizability. They also do not fully exclude effect modification by batch in magnitude, because the tests are direct stratum estimates rather than formal interactions with multiplicity-adjusted confidence intervals. However, none of the four associations disappears or reverses across the three remaining batches. Since no voluntary validation requests remain, the evidence should be interpreted as strong internal reproducibility, not independent external validation. All twelve claims are closed as accepted internal associations.

Study instructions:
Investigate diverse, scientifically meaningful comparisons and use previous
results to allocate further investigation. Broad exploration and focused follow-up are both useful
throughout the run. Assess discoveries in this supplied dataset and use independent validation when
useful. Biological interpretation and generalizability may remain uncertain.

Register comparisons, anticipated directions, and initial assessments before requesting analyses.
The controller assigns claim references. For a changed claim, propose a new comparison and link
refinements to the earlier parent claim.
Clinical log_pfs_months is natural log progression-free survival in months, fully observed without
censoring. Dependency scores are continuous; more negative values mean stronger dependency.
Research signatures are constructed standardized assays in arbitrary units. Research markers D, E,
and F are constructed binary assays with no assigned gene, pathway, or clinical role.
A mean_difference is exposed minus comparator within eligibility and subgroup. An interaction
subtracts that comparison in the subgroup complement in the same eligible population.
Use your scientific judgment to assess the size, uncertainty, and importance of each effect
and decide which conclusions the evidence supports. Explain your reasoning in the narrative.
Returned estimates and intervals are ALREADY SIGNED to the indicated hypothesis direction. Do not
multiply them by direction again. For example, raw -0.4 with direction -1 is reported as +0.4.
Discovery analyses use 95% Welch intervals and need at least 20 observations in every
comparison cell.

Each iteration has explore, analyze, appraise, and synthesize stages. Every stage may register
hypotheses for later analysis. Analyze selects up to 12 previously registered hypotheses.
Appraise assesses every new discovery result, records active/deferred/closed investigation, and may
request validation after considering those results. At most one new voluntary validation request
is allowed per iteration and ten per run. Cached requests reuse the same evidence. The evaluator
may also deliver scheduled validation during the run. Independent intervals account for the maximum
number of validation comparisons in the run. Results arrive before synthesis. Assess newly released
validation immediately in synthesis and explicitly reassess the original claim when its response
deadline appears in the context, even if you also investigate a refinement. The controller maintains
the accepted claim set from your assessments; you do not need to repeat that list. Explanations are
retained for inspection. Acceptance does not require prior independent validation.


You are investigating the supplied research dataset. Return one JSON object using
only this stage's response form. The service performs analyses; you choose the science.
For this task, a relative difference in outcome of 10% or greater is considered clinically significant.
Use your judgment about uncertainty and conclusions in light of this clinical significance threshold. Acceptance does not require
independent validation first. Explain your reasoning in narrative.

The ledger contains every registered claim, its current assessment, and all its available direct
evidence. References H1, H2, ... identify claims; R1, R2, ... identify evidence. Copy these short
references when needed. New proposals receive references automatically after this stage. A changed
comparison or reversed claim is a new proposal, optionally linked to an existing parent.
Proposal direction is the claim (+1 positive, -1 negative); anticipated_direction is your
expectation
of the raw exposed-minus-comparator contrast before seeing evidence (-1, 0 uncertain, +1).
initial_status is your assessment at registration. These initial judgments are recorded once.
If a proposal repeats an existing claim, the controller preserves that claim's current assessment;
use assessments to change a scientific conclusion.

For each claim in assessments_due, return one assessment with claim,
status (accept/reject/unresolved),
and investigation (active/deferred/closed). You may also reassess other claims. Omitted claims keep
their current assessment. Assess the original claim even when proposing a refinement or reversal.
By omitting evidence in an assessment, you assess all evidence displayed on that claim's card;
the controller attaches those references. To specify a subset or related evidence, provide evidence

An unchanged assessment or an investigation-only change can use evidence: [];

For a refinement, parent identifies the earlier claim; omitted motivating_evidence attaches the

The final scientific conclusions are based on the accumulated unadjusted discovery tests in the supplied lung-lineage dataset plus the independent validations already completed for selected claims. These are internal associations, not causal claims or generalizable therapeutic claims. Because dependency scores are continuous and often centered below zero, relative percent differences near zero are unstable; I used a conservative absolute signed dependency-score benchmark of about 0.10 as the practical marker of scientific meaningfulness, with all estimates already signed to the registered hypothesis direction. For direction -1, a positive estimate means the exposed or subgroup contrast is more negative and therefore stronger dependency; for direction +1, a positive estimate means less negative and therefore weaker dependency.

SUPPORTED ROBUST FINDINGS. First, SMARCA4 loss is associated with much stronger SMARCA2 dependency. Core evidence H6/R6 is +0.784 [0.765,0.803]; independent validation R53 is +0.804 [0.775,0.833]. This is the strongest signal and remains robust across many internal eligibility strata including lineage subtype, library, screen quality, ploidy, mutation burden, Cas9 activity, culture, age, and co-mutation-negative contexts. Second, MSI-high status is associated with much stronger WRN dependency. Core evidence H7/R7 is +0.790 [0.760,0.819]; validation R40 is +0.812 [0.765,0.858], and it persists in TP53-loss context H83/R60 validated by R79. It also replicates across batch strata R294-R296. Third, KEAP1 loss is associated with weaker NFE2L2 dependency, reversing the original hypothesis. H8/R8 is rejected; the reverse accepted claim H13/R8 is +0.796 [0.776,0.816], with validation R66 +0.791 [0.763,0.820]. This is large and reproducible but biologically opposite the original expectation and requires cautious interpretation. Fourth, PTEN loss is associated with stronger STAT3 dependency. Core evidence H41/R25 is +0.267 [0.215,0.319]; validation R26 is +0.268 [0.188,0.348]. It is reproduced across many strata and batch tests R300-R302; direct EMT strata are strong with R284 +0.411 [0.219,0.603] and R285 +0.253 [0.199,0.307]. Fifth, TP53 loss is associated with weaker USP7 dependency. Discovery evidence H24/R293 and equivalent reverse-coded H216/R293 is +0.802 [0.782,0.822]. This association is strong internally and replicates in batch strata R303-R305, but because the validation budget is exhausted it remains unvalidated and should be viewed as requiring external replication. Additional supported but more stratum-specific findings include PTEN loss/STAT3 dependency in PIK3CA-mutant lines H70/R46 +0.268 [0.127,0.409], validated by R106 +0.294 [0.069,0.519], and STK11 loss/STAT3 dependency in age >= 65 H253/R241 +0.258 [0.133,0.382], which remains hypothesis generating because the overall STK11/STAT3 test was null and this subgroup was not independently validated.

NEGATIVE FINDINGS. Many simple matched-genotype or pathway addiction hypotheses are unsupported. KRAS mutation did not show stronger KRAS dependency (H1/R1 +0.014 [-0.004,0.031]); BRAF V600E did not show stronger BRAF dependency (H2/R2 -0.017 [-0.045,0.012]); EGFR amplification was null and independently validated (H3/R3 +0.025 [-0.000,0.051], R13 +0.002 [-0.043,0.046]); ERBB2 amplification was null (H4/R4); TP53 loss did not show stronger MDM2 dependency (H5/R5). ARID1A loss did not show stronger SMARCA2 dependency, with discovery R15 and validation R80 null; RB1 loss did not show stronger POLR2A dependency, with discovery R23 and validation R39 null. MYC amplification hypotheses for DHX9, POLR2A, MDM2, KRAS, and STAT3 were generally null or far below benchmark, including R10, R11, R34, R73, and R123. Final smaller negative tests include APC mutation versus TMED10 dependency R75 and BRAF V600E versus RIT1 dependency R77. Some discovery-positive effects were not validated: the culture adherent interaction for WRN/MSI-high H112 had discovery R94 +0.105 but validation R105 -0.019 [-0.148,0.111]; PTEN loss in KRAS-mutant lines versus KRAS dependency H131 had discovery R115 +0.064 [0.020,0.108] but validation R119 -0.030 [-0.105,0.045]; the SLFN11-high WRN/MSI interaction had discovery R122 +0.057 but validation R132 -0.016 [-0.121,0.090]. Formal effect modification by EMT was not established despite strong direct EMT stratum estimates, including H288/R283 +0.158 [-0.040,0.357], and high mutation burden did not support PTEN/STAT3 interaction R286 +0.012 [-0.101,0.125].

UNRESOLVED UNCERTAINTY. The main unresolved items are not likely to change the five core internal associations but do limit specificity and generalizability. PTEN-loss/STAT3 interaction by high ploidy remains unresolved: H285/R263 +0.033 [-0.082,0.149]. The broader EMT >= 0.5 interaction is also not decisive: H116/R98 +0.117 [-0.006,0.241]. Adenocarcinoma and PIK3CA-stratum PTEN/STAT3 interactions H44/R28 and H45/R282 are wide and unresolved. Several environmental or clinical interactions remain unresolved because their intervals still include meaningful values: media serum H103/R85 +0.047 [-0.057,0.151], culture H114/R96 -0.023 [-0.149,0.104], sex H232/R221 +0.073 [-0.031,0.177], growth-rate strata H237/R226 +0.035 [-0.092,0.162] and H241/R230 +0.042 [-0.071,0.156], age interaction H244/R233 +0.124 [-0.023,0.270], WRN batch interaction H208/R198 +0.048 [-0.019,0.115], WRN TP53 interaction H222/R211 +0.053 [-0.022,0.127], and NFE2L2 growth-rate interaction H224/R213 +0.051 [0.001,0.101]. Non-Avana PTEN/STAT3 H197/R187 is unresolved with +0.092 [-0.062,0.246]. Invalid small-cell tests, including R189, R195, R196, R203, and R275, are noninformative rather than evidence against association. Finally, the TP53-loss/USP7 association and the STK11-loss/STAT3 age-stratum finding need external validation; all accepted claims remain unadjusted associations within this dataset.

MOST INFORMATIVE NEXT ANALYSIS. Because the independent validation budget is exhausted and the major mean-difference signals have already been resolved, the best next step is not more broad unadjusted mean-difference testing in the same dataset. The most informative follow-up would be independent external validation or a pre-specified adjusted analysis of the five core associations, especially PTEN loss versus STAT3 dependency and TP53 loss versus USP7 dependency, with covariate adjustment for batch, library, screen QC, ploidy, and co-mutations. If one within-dataset interaction question must be prioritized, a model-based or carefully powered analysis of EMT status and ploidy modifying PTEN-loss/STAT3 dependency is most informative, because direct stratum estimates are strong but interaction intervals remain wide. Overall, the defensible final conclusions are five internal associations: SMARCA4 loss with stronger SMARCA2 dependency, MSI-high with stronger WRN dependency, KEAP1 loss with weaker NFE2L2 dependency, PTEN loss with stronger STAT3 dependency, and TP53 loss with weaker USP7 dependency, with the last not independently validated. Many negative and unresolved results should be retained as part of the evidence about what was tested and what remains uncertain in this dataset.
